Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.

Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.

Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.

The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.
After the shove, the humiliation flushes into rage, with his hand going to the hilt. It stays a petulant prince, not a cartoon.
Royal Guards: Impassive and disciplined. "Aadesh Yuvraj" is clipped and dutiful, and they draw in unison.

  "text": "Emotional Target: Toxic provocation met with icy moral defiance.
Atmosphere Direction: Claustrophobic, hostile, volatile.
Camera Intent:
Opening: A slow crane down from the vault onto the glowing seven-gate hologram, with Devika turning the compass and Agnivesh leaning in (2).
The entrance: The doors burst open on a snap push-in (fast beat 1, 3). Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh on a slow circular track (4).

A low-angle tilt up on Ranvijay waving the map away (9).
A slow tilt down finds Agnivesh's fist and the glow through his sleeve (7).
A slow track-out ahead of Ranvijay as he grips the hilt and advances toward the lens, so he grows in frame and the move ends behind Agnivesh's shoulder for the over-the-shoulder (14).
Devika: A crane down from the violet seal to Devika (8), then a high arc around the table as she points to the gates (10).
The lips: A track with Ranvijay up the left side into a profile two-shot of his finger on Devika's lips (11).
The shove: A handheld-energy push (fast beat 2, 12).
The guards: Agnivesh's reply is a static hold (16). The guards are summoned on a high crane-back (17).
Devika parts them: A low-angle push-in as Devika parts the brothers (18). A top-down crane as the hologram collapses into the map (19). A tilt up as she folds it and walks out through the archway (20).

The table runs from the double doors at the near end to the shelves and stone archway at the far end.
Devika stands at the far end facing the doors. Agnivesh is at the table's right side.
Ranvijay enters from the doors, circles behind Agnivesh to the near end, then walks up the left side to Devika.
The guards halt just inside the doorway, then draw and stride up to stand behind Ranvijay.
Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.
Acting Notes:
Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.
On the finger on Devika's lips, a flash in the eyes, then decisive action. The shove is functional, not theatrical.
Afterwards he is completely still again. The rebuke is level and cutting, not shouted.
Devika:
Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.
When Ranvijay touches her lips, she goes still with cold eyes: no flinch, no melodrama.
She parts the brothers with a firm, economical push, and her line is quiet and pointed.
Ranvijay:
The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.

  "text": "Emotional Target: Toxic provocation met with icy moral defiance.
Atmosphere Direction: Claustrophobic, hostile, volatile.
Camera Intent:
Opening: A slow crane down from the vault onto the glowing seven-gate hologram, with Devika turning the compass and Agnivesh leaning in (2).
The entrance: The doors burst open on a snap push-in (fast beat 1, 3). Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh on a slow circular track (4).

Over-the-shoulder shots and dolly-ins carry the insults (5, 6, 13, 15).
A low-angle tilt up on Ranvijay waving the map away (9).
A slow tilt down finds Agnivesh's fist and the glow through his sleeve (7).
A slow track-out ahead of Ranvijay as he grips the hilt and advances toward the lens, so he grows in frame and the move ends behind Agnivesh's shoulder for the over-the-shoulder (14).
Devika: A crane down from the violet seal to Devika (8), then a high arc around the table as she points to the gates (10).
The lips: A track with Ranvijay up the left side into a profile two-shot of his finger on Devika's lips (11).
The shove: A handheld-energy push (fast beat 2, 12).
The guards: Agnivesh's reply is a static hold (16). The guards are summoned on a high crane-back (17).
Devika parts them: A low-angle push-in as Devika parts the brothers (18). A top-down crane as the hologram collapses into the map (19). A tilt up as she folds it and walks out through the archway (20).
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The table runs from the double doors at the near end to the shelves and stone archway at the far end.
Devika stands at the far end facing the doors. Agnivesh is at the table's right side.
Ranvijay enters from the doors, circles behind Agnivesh to the near end, then walks up the left side to Devika.
The guards halt just inside the doorway, then draw and stride up to stand behind Ranvijay.
Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.
Acting Notes:
Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.
On the finger on Devika's lips, a flash in the eyes, then decisive action. The shove is functional, not theatrical.
Afterwards he is completely still again. The rebuke is level and cutting, not shouted.
Devika:
Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.
When Ranvijay touches her lips, she goes still with cold eyes: no flinch, no melodrama.
She parts the brothers with a firm, economical push, and her line is quiet and pointed.
Ranvijay:
The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.
After the shove, the humiliation flushes into rage, with his hand going to the hilt. It stays a petulant prince, not a cartoon.
Royal Guards: Impassive and disciplined. "Aadesh Yuvraj" is clipped and dutiful, and they draw in unison.

Native 9:16: Every shot is composed for 9:16 vertical, with all characters fully inside frame. Every camera note ends with "9:16 vertical composition, all characters fully inside frame".

The archive's bookshelves and stone archway, the corridor's stone walls and pillars, and the chamber doorway and dome ribs box in Ranvijay and his guards.

Symmetry vs. Diagonal Conflict:
Symmetry is held during the ritual reading of the Celestial Ward Map, to show ancestral order.

Foreground: Physical barriers: carved table corners, hovering hologram light, the relic's rings, sword hilts.

Background: Deep perspective of the stone vaults, library stacks, guarded doorways and the dome. Guards sit here, stacked in depth.

  "heading": "Scene 4: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 23–46 / 132s)",
  "text": "Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).
The reaction (25): A two-shot from the map looking up, Devika's face in the top third and Agnivesh's in the bottom third, lit gold from below by the turning relic rings with the dark dome between them. A slow push-in with a gentle rack focus from Agnivesh to Devika.
A low tilt and crane up as the hologram blooms into the dome (26).
A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).
A tilt down to the spinning compass (29).
The collapse (30): A crane down as the hologram streams into the relic.
The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).
The draw (35–36): An overhead as the guards close in (35). The draw, with a snap push-in to the blade at the throat (fast beat 3, 36).
The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).
A slow crane down past the blade in the foreground to Devika's raised palm and face (38).
A slow arc around Ranvijay for the tirade (39).
A slow push-in as Agnivesh steps into the blade and the nick appears (40).
A low-angle medium wide on Ranvijay's trembling sword arm, the guards watching from behind in depth, on a slow tilt up (41).
The finger (42–44): Starting close on the finger on the blade and the glowing wrist mark, a slow arc track-out reveals his calm face and the sunstone (42). A track-out as the sword swings down and Ranvijay stumbles (43). A static low angle on "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third."

 "continuity_section": "⑥ Transitions & Visual Continuity

Inter-Scene Transitions:

Ep 1 to Scene 1: Ep 1 ends on the hard cut on the glowing wrist mark. Ep 2 opens directly on the daylight palace time-lapse.
Scene 1 to Scene 2: Match dissolve from the palace's central dome under the full moon into the archive's vaulted ceiling, where the crane down in shot 2 begins.
Scene 2 to Scene 3: Straight cut, following Devika's stride as she walks out through the stone archway at the back of the archive.
Scene 3 to Scene 4: A continuous flow cut as the procession steps through the chamber doorway.
Scene 4 Climax: A crash zoom onto the violet symbol pulsing in the dark, then HARD CUT to black. No freeze-frame, no fade.

Visual Continuity Anchors:

Agnivesh's Attire:
His exact Ep 1 outfit throughout: fitted deep royal-blue silk angrakha with full-length sleeves and gold zari cuffs, sleek polished silver-and-gold breastplate with engraved lotus-vine patterns and the sun-mandala boss, layered silver shoulder guards, engraved silver-and-gold waist guard, ivory silk dhoti with a gold border, maroon silk angavastram draped from one shoulder, single pearl mala, tall leather boots with silver shin guards, and the scorched right cuff. No scabbard, no weapon.
No scabbard and no weapon in any shot.
The Ancient Book does not appear in Ep 2; his hands stay free throughout.
Devika's Attire: Turquoise-and-gold warrior attire with only Devika's Dagger at her belt. The Dual Short-Swords do not appear in Ep 2.
The Ancestral Sword:
Sc 2: thrust through Ranvijay's sash, hilt at his right hand.
Sc 3: sheathed in his right hand, scabbard tip dragging.
Sc 4: slid back into the sash on entering, then drawn right-handed to Agnivesh's throat, swung down, and raised for the charge.
Ranvijay's own talwar stays in its dark-red scabbard at his left hip and is never drawn.
Devika's Tools:
Sc 2: compass in hand. She sets it on the table before parting the brothers, then picks it up again.
Sc 3: the folded map and the compass in her hands.
Sc 4: the map unrolled over the relic, the compass open on the floor by her right knee, picked up in her left hand when she rises.
The Mark:
From the first archive shot: the scorched right cuff is already pulled down over the hidden mark (time has passed since Ep 1, bridged by the time-lapse).
Sc 2: a faint glow pulsing through the silk only (7); the cuff stays down.
Sc 4: the sleeve slides back and the mark glows gold as the sunstone answers (42).
The Wound: A thin line of blood at the front-left of Agnivesh's throat, below the jaw, from the moment he steps into the blade (40) until the end.
Light:
Sc 1: day turning to moonlit night.
Sc 2 to Sc 4: night lamp and torchlight plus the hologram glow.
After the gutter, the violet glow is the only light.",

  "heading": "Scene 4: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 23–46 / 132s)",
  "text": "Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).
The reaction (25): A two-shot from the map looking up, Devika's face in the top third and Agnivesh's in the bottom third, lit gold from below by the turning relic rings with the dark dome between them. A slow push-in with a gentle rack focus from Agnivesh to Devika.
A low tilt and crane up as the hologram blooms into the dome (26).
A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).
A tilt down to the spinning compass (29).
The collapse (30): A crane down as the hologram streams into the relic.
The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).
The draw (35–36): An overhead as the guards close in (35). The draw, with a snap push-in to the blade at the throat (fast beat 3, 36).
The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).
A slow crane down past the blade in the foreground to Devika's raised palm and face (38).
A slow arc around Ranvijay for the tirade (39).
A slow push-in as Agnivesh steps into the blade and the nick appears (40).
A low-angle medium wide on Ranvijay's trembling sword arm, the guards watching from behind in depth, on a slow tilt up (41).
The finger (42–44): Starting close on the finger on the blade and the glowing wrist mark, a slow arc track-out reveals his calm face and the sunstone (42). A track-out as the sword swings down and Ranvijay stumbles (43). A static low angle on "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third."

 "continuity_section": "⑥ Transitions & Visual Continuity

Inter-Scene Transitions:

Ep 1 to Scene 1: Ep 1 ends on the hard cut on the glowing wrist mark. Ep 2 opens directly on the daylight palace time-lapse.
Scene 1 to Scene 2: Match dissolve from the palace's central dome under the full moon into the archive's vaulted ceiling, where the crane down in shot 2 begins.
Scene 2 to Scene 3: Straight cut, following Devika's stride as she walks out through the stone archway at the back of the archive.
Scene 3 to Scene 4: A continuous flow cut as the procession steps through the chamber doorway.
Scene 4 Climax: A crash zoom onto the violet symbol pulsing in the dark, then HARD CUT to black. No freeze-frame, no fade.

Visual Continuity Anchors:

Agnivesh's Attire:
His exact Ep 1 outfit throughout: fitted deep royal-blue silk angrakha with full-length sleeves and gold zari cuffs, sleek polished silver-and-gold breastplate with engraved lotus-vine patterns and the sun-mandala boss, layered silver shoulder guards, engraved silver-and-gold waist guard, ivory silk dhoti with a gold border, maroon silk angavastram draped from one shoulder, single pearl mala, tall leather boots with silver shin guards, and the scorched right cuff. No scabbard, no weapon.
No scabbard and no weapon in any shot.
The Ancient Book does not appear in Ep 2; his hands stay free throughout.
Devika's Attire: Turquoise-and-gold warrior attire with only Devika's Dagger at her belt. The Dual Short-Swords do not appear in Ep 2.
The Ancestral Sword:
Sc 2: thrust through Ranvijay's sash, hilt at his right hand.
Sc 3: sheathed in his right hand, scabbard tip dragging.
Sc 4: slid back into the sash on entering, then drawn right-handed to Agnivesh's throat, swung down, and raised for the charge.
Ranvijay's own talwar stays in its dark-red scabbard at his left hip and is never drawn.
Devika's Tools:
Sc 2: compass in hand. She sets it on the table before parting the brothers, then picks it up again.
Sc 3: the folded map and the compass in her hands.
Sc 4: the map unrolled over the relic, the compass open on the floor by her right knee, picked up in her left hand when she rises.
The Mark:
From the first archive shot: the scorched right cuff is already pulled down over the hidden mark (time has passed since Ep 1, bridged by the time-lapse).
Sc 2: a faint glow pulsing through the silk only (7); the cuff stays down.
Sc 4: the sleeve slides back and the mark glows gold as the sunstone answers (42).
The Wound: A thin line of blood at the front-left of Agnivesh's throat, below the jaw, from the moment he steps into the blade (40) until the end.
Light:
Sc 1: day turning to moonlit night.
Sc 2 to Sc 4: night lamp and torchlight plus the hologram glow.
After the gutter, the violet glow is the only light.",

  "text": "Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).
The reaction (25): A two-shot from the map looking up, Devika's face in the top third and Agnivesh's in the bottom third, lit gold from below by the turning relic rings with the dark dome between them. A slow push-in with a gentle rack focus from Agnivesh to Devika.
A low tilt and crane up as the hologram blooms into the dome (26).
A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).
A tilt down to the spinning compass (29).
The collapse (30): A crane down as the hologram streams into the relic.
The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).
The draw (35–36): An overhead as the guards close in (35). The draw, with a snap push-in to the blade at the throat (fast beat 3, 36).
The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).
A slow crane down past the blade in the foreground to Devika's raised palm and face (38).
A slow arc around Ranvijay for the tirade (39).
A slow push-in as Agnivesh steps into the blade and the nick appears (40).
A low-angle medium wide on Ranvijay's trembling sword arm, the guards watching from behind in depth, on a slow tilt up (41).
The finger (42–44): Starting close on the finger on the blade and the glowing wrist mark, a slow arc track-out reveals his calm face and the sunstone (42). A track-out as the sword swings down and Ranvijay stumbles (43). A static low angle on "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third."

 "continuity_section": "⑥ Transitions & Visual Continuity

Inter-Scene Transitions:

Ep 1 to Scene 1: Ep 1 ends on the hard cut on the glowing wrist mark. Ep 2 opens directly on the daylight palace time-lapse.
Scene 1 to Scene 2: Match dissolve from the palace's central dome under the full moon into the archive's vaulted ceiling, where the crane down in shot 2 begins.

Scene 3 to Scene 4: A continuous flow cut as the procession steps through the chamber doorway.
Scene 4 Climax: A crash zoom onto the violet symbol pulsing in the dark, then HARD CUT to black. No freeze-frame, no fade.

Visual Continuity Anchors:

Agnivesh's Attire:
His exact Ep 1 outfit throughout: fitted deep royal-blue silk angrakha with full-length sleeves and gold zari cuffs, sleek polished silver-and-gold breastplate with engraved lotus-vine patterns and the sun-mandala boss, layered silver shoulder guards, engraved silver-and-gold waist guard, ivory silk dhoti with a gold border, maroon silk angavastram draped from one shoulder, single pearl mala, tall leather boots with silver shin guards, and the scorched right cuff. No scabbard, no weapon.
No scabbard and no weapon in any shot.
The Ancient Book does not appear in Ep 2; his hands stay free throughout.
Devika's Attire: Turquoise-and-gold warrior attire with only Devika's Dagger at her belt. The Dual Short-Swords do not appear in Ep 2.
The Ancestral Sword:
Sc 2: thrust through Ranvijay's sash, hilt at his right hand.
Sc 3: sheathed in his right hand, scabbard tip dragging.
Sc 4: slid back into the sash on entering, then drawn right-handed to Agnivesh's throat, swung down, and raised for the charge.
Ranvijay's own talwar stays in its dark-red scabbard at his left hip and is never drawn.
Devika's Tools:
Sc 2: compass in hand. She sets it on the table before parting the brothers, then picks it up again.
Sc 3: the folded map and the compass in her hands.
Sc 4: the map unrolled over the relic, the compass open on the floor by her right knee, picked up in her left hand when she rises.
The Mark:
From the first archive shot: the scorched right cuff is already pulled down over the hidden mark (time has passed since Ep 1, bridged by the time-lapse).
Sc 2: a faint glow pulsing through the silk only (7); the cuff stays down.
Sc 4: the sleeve slides back and the mark glows gold as the sunstone answers (42).
The Wound: A thin line of blood at the front-left of Agnivesh's throat, below the jaw, from the moment he steps into the blade (40) until the end.
Light:
Sc 1: day turning to moonlit night.
Sc 2 to Sc 4: night lamp and torchlight plus the hologram glow.

  "text": "Emotional Target: The court's fear turned into blame; a public verdict without a trial.\nAtmosphere Direction: Ominous, windswept, the sky breaking overhead.\nCamera Intent:\nThe sky (1–2): a follow shot along the leading edge of the crack (Raksha-Kavach Cracked (Violet Thunder)), first frame matching Ep 3's last frames; a slow pull back over the citadel (Suryagarh Citadel).\nThe court (3): a slow crane up the steps from the lower steps (Temple Steps, Low Angle).\nThe plant (4): a slow push-in on Badrinath, hands folded, no staff.\nThe accusation (5): a slow arc as Someshwar turns to the guards and points.\nThe grip (6): a slow push-in from the king's eyeline down onto Agnivesh, the city behind.\nThe plea and the reply (7–8): low push-in on Devika; a slow dolly back as Someshwar takes one step down toward her.\nThe exit (9): a slow crane up and back over Ranvijay's shoulder as the procession crosses the citadel toward the tower.\nSpatial Staging & Distance: Someshwar at the top, Badrinath at his shoulder, Ranvijay beside them (screen-left, top); Agnivesh held a few steps below (Guard 1 on his left arm, Guard 2 on his right), screen-right; Devika on the steps between the two groups; Royal Courtiers in depth by the doors. SCENE: Scene 2: INT. ROYAL ARCHIVES - NIGHT (Shots 2–20 / 117s)
Emotional Target: Toxic provocation met with icy moral defiance.
Atmosphere Direction: Claustrophobic, hostile, volatile.
Camera Intent:
Opening: A slow crane down from the vault onto the glowing seven-gate hologram, with Devika turning the compass and Agnivesh leaning in (2).
The entrance: The doors burst open on a snap push-in (fast beat 1, 3). Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh on a slow circular track (4).
The insults:
Over-the-shoulder shots and dolly-ins carry the insults (5, 6, 13, 15).
A low-angle tilt up on Ranvijay waving the map away (9).
A slow tilt down finds Agnivesh's fist and the glow through his sleeve (7).
A slow track-out ahead of Ranvijay as he grips the hilt and advances toward the lens, so he grows in frame and the move ends behind Agnivesh's shoulder for the over-the-shoulder (14).
Devika: A crane down from the violet seal to Devika (8), then a high arc around the table as she points to the gates (10).
The lips: A track with Ranvijay up the left side into a profile two-shot of his finger on Devika's lips (11).
The shove: A handheld-energy push (fast beat 2, 12).
The guards: Agnivesh's reply is a static hold (16). The guards are summoned on a high crane-back (17).
Devika parts them: A low-angle push-in as Devika parts the brothers (18). A top-down crane as the hologram collapses into the map (19). A tilt up as she folds it and walks out through the archway (20).
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The table runs from the double doors at the near end to the shelves and stone archway at the far end.
Devika stands at the far end facing the doors. Agnivesh is at the table's right side.
Ranvijay enters from the doors, circles behind Agnivesh to the near end, then walks up the left side to Devika.
The guards halt just inside the doorway, then draw and stride up to stand behind Ranvijay.
Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.
Acting Notes:
Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.
On the finger on Devika's lips, a flash in the eyes, then decisive action. The shove is functional, not theatrical.
Afterwards he is completely still again. The rebuke is level and cutting, not shouted.
Devika:
Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.
When Ranvijay touches her lips, she goes still with cold eyes: no flinch, no melodrama.
She parts the brothers with a firm, economical push, and her line is quiet and pointed.
Ranvijay:
The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.
After the shove, the humiliation flushes into rage, with his hand going to the hilt. It stays a petulant prince, not a cartoon.
Royal Guards: Impassive and disciplined. "Aadesh Yuvraj" is clipped and dutiful, and they draw in unison.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Royal Archives plate: brass oil lamps and wall torches as the warm, flickering key, with deep moody shadows and floating dust in the shafts of light.
The hologram: A motivated soft gold source from table height, uplighting Devika's and Agnivesh's faces and catching the brass instruments.
The violet flicker: The flickering northern seal throws a faint violet pulse onto Devika's face (2, 8).
The doors: The burst sends a draught that makes the torch flames flare and shadows jump (3).
The collapse: When the hologram collapses (19), the gold fill drops away and the faces fall back to lamp and torchlight only.
Faces: Lit by the same flicker and colour temperature as the set, with real contact shadows on the table and floor.

Emotional Target: Toxic provocation met with icy moral defiance.
Atmosphere Direction: Claustrophobic, hostile, volatile.
Camera Intent:
Opening: A slow crane down from the vault onto the glowing seven-gate hologram, with Devika turning the compass and Agnivesh leaning in (2).
The entrance: The doors burst open on a snap push-in (fast beat 1, 3). Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh on a slow circular track (4).
The insults:
Over-the-shoulder shots and dolly-ins carry the insults (5, 6, 13, 15).
A low-angle tilt up on Ranvijay waving the map away (9).
A slow tilt down finds Agnivesh's fist and the glow through his sleeve (7).
A slow track-out ahead of Ranvijay as he grips the hilt and advances toward the lens, so he grows in frame and the move ends behind Agnivesh's shoulder for the over-the-shoulder (14).
Devika: A crane down from the violet seal to Devika (8), then a high arc around the table as she points to the gates (10).
The lips: A track with Ranvijay up the left side into a profile two-shot of his finger on Devika's lips (11).
The shove: A handheld-energy push (fast beat 2, 12).
The guards: Agnivesh's reply is a static hold (16). The guards are summoned on a high crane-back (17).
Devika parts them: A low-angle push-in as Devika parts the brothers (18). A top-down crane as the hologram collapses into the map (19). A tilt up as she folds it and walks out through the archway (20).
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The table runs from the double doors at the near end to the shelves and stone archway at the far end.
Devika stands at the far end facing the doors. Agnivesh is at the table's right side.
Ranvijay enters from the doors, circles behind Agnivesh to the near end, then walks up the left side to Devika.
The guards halt just inside the doorway, then draw and stride up to stand behind Ranvijay.
Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.
Acting Notes:
Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.
On the finger on Devika's lips, a flash in the eyes, then decisive action. The shove is functional, not theatrical.
Afterwards he is completely still again. The rebuke is level and cutting, not shouted.
Devika:
Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.

Ranvijay:
The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.
After the shove, the humiliation flushes into rage, with his hand going to the hilt. It stays a petulant prince, not a cartoon.
Royal Guards: Impassive and disciplined. "Aadesh Yuvraj" is clipped and dutiful, and they draw in unison.

Base light: Match the Royal Archives plate: brass oil lamps and wall torches as the warm, flickering key, with deep moody shadows and floating dust in the shafts of light.
The hologram: A motivated soft gold source from table height, uplighting Devika's and Agnivesh's faces and catching the brass instruments.
The violet flicker: The flickering northern seal throws a faint violet pulse onto Devika's face (2, 8).
The doors: The burst sends a draught that makes the torch flames flare and shadows jump (3).
The collapse: When the hologram collapses (19), the gold fill drops away and the faces fall back to lamp and torchlight only.
Faces: Lit by the same flicker and colour temperature as the set, with real contact shadows on the table and floor.

SCENE: Scene 4: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 23–46 / 132s)
Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).
The reaction (25): A two-shot from the map looking up, Devika's face in the top third and Agnivesh's in the bottom third, lit gold from below by the turning relic rings with the dark dome between them. A slow push-in with a gentle rack focus from Agnivesh to Devika.
A low tilt and crane up as the hologram blooms into the dome (26).
A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).
A tilt down to the spinning compass (29).
The collapse (30): A crane down as the hologram streams into the relic.
The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).
The draw (35–36): An overhead as the guards close in (35). The draw, with a snap push-in to the blade at the throat (fast beat 3, 36).
The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).
A slow crane down past the blade in the foreground to Devika's raised palm and face (38).
A slow arc around Ranvijay for the tirade (39).
A slow push-in as Agnivesh steps into the blade and the nick appears (40).
A low-angle medium wide on Ranvijay's trembling sword arm, the guards watching from behind in depth, on a slow tilt up (41).
The finger (42–44): Starting close on the finger on the blade and the glowing wrist mark, a slow arc track-out reveals his calm face and the sunstone (42). A track-out as the sword swings down and Ranvijay stumbles (43). A static low angle on "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third.

SCENE: Scene 4: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 23–46 / 132s)
Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).
The reaction (25): A two-shot from the map looking up, Devika's face in the top third and Agnivesh's in the bottom third, lit gold from below by the turning relic rings with the dark dome between them. A slow push-in with a gentle rack focus from Agnivesh to Devika.
A low tilt and crane up as the hologram blooms into the dome (26).
A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).
A tilt down to the spinning compass (29).
The collapse (30): A crane down as the hologram streams into the relic.
The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).
The draw (35–36): An overhead as the guards close in (35). The draw, with a snap push-in to the blade at the throat (fast beat 3, 36).
The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).
A slow crane down past the blade in the foreground to Devika's raised palm and face (38).
A slow arc around Ranvijay for the tirade (39).
A slow push-in as Agnivesh steps into the blade and the nick appears (40).
A low-angle medium wide on Ranvijay's trembling sword arm, the guards watching from behind in depth, on a slow tilt up (41).
The finger (42–44): Starting close on the finger on the blade and the glowing wrist mark, a slow arc track-out reveals his calm face and the sunstone (42). A track-out as the sword swings down and Ranvijay stumbles (43). A static low angle on "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third.

EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY A circular sand arena ringed by carved stone stands, sun-emblem banners everywhere. The royal throne canopy stands on a raised marble dais at the north end, overlooking the arena; directly beside it is a separate covered stand where the royal courtiers sit. Citizens crowd the stone stands on the other sides, and the grand entrance gate is at the south end, facing the throne. Citizens wear simple cotton dhotis and sarees; courtiers wear silk angavastrams and turbans. Characters: Prince Ranvijay, Ranvijay's Horse, Rajguru Badrinath, Maharaja Someshwar, Several Royal Courtiers, Several Citizens A ROYAL GONG crashes. Citizens press against the arena railing and raise sun-emblem flags. PRINCE RANVIJAY (early 20s, fair-to-wheatish skin, broad shoulders, wearing golden royal armour and a small crownlet) rides into the arena on RANVIJAY'S HORSE (a jet-black Marwari stallion, red-and-gold saddle cloth). He trots across the sand toward the north end. Brass bells on the reins ring. Ranvijay raises his jeweled sword toward the crowd. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Dekho dekho kaun aaya...Suryagarh ka sher aaya...Rajkumar Ranvijay ki jay, Rajkumar Ranvijay ki jay Prince Ranvijay halts his horse in front of the royal courtier seating area and looks towards the stand. PRINCE RANVIJAY (booming, playful) Dekha, rajguru? mere aagman bhar se hi praja mein sahas aur utsaah ki lahar daud gayi.. Standing at the front rail of the courtiers' stand, closest to the throne dais, is RAJGURU BADRINATH (60s, bald, flame-and-lotus scalp tattoo, white beard, saffron robes, rudraksha beads) who raises both hands toward Ranvijay. RAJGURU BADRINATH (smooth, ceremonial) ye toh hona hi tha rajkumar, sampoorna rajya is baat ko bhalibhati jaanta hai ki Swarnadweep ke asli rakshak aap hi hai. PRINCE RANVIJAY (loud, smug) rakshak nahi rajguru ..main is rajya ka hone wala samraat hun aur ye praja meri daas... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (60s, dusky skin, weathered face, gold robes and silver beard) sits on his throne on the raised dais beneath the sun-carved canopy, just beside the courtiers' stand, looking down at Ranvijay. He strikes the armrest with his ring. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, formal) swagat kijiye aapke hone wale samraat ka.. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR points his hands towards Ranvijay, Their eyes meet and both smile. The citizens start cheering his name again. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jay! Ranvijay raises his hands and takes their appreciation. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, formal) Poore rajya mein koi hai jo Yuvraj Ranvijay ko chunauti de sake? EXT. RAJMAHAL - DAY (CONTINUOUS) We see the sprawling view of a grand royal palace with endless rooms. INT. RAJMAHAL - AGNIVESH'S READING ROOM - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh A quiet room filled with bookshelves lined with ancient books. AGNIVESH (24, royal-blue angrakha, ivory dhoti, maroon angavastram, worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist) sits in shadow by a narrow window, slowly turning the pages of an ancient book. Hearing the distant roar from the arena, Agnivesh closes the book, rises and walks out through the hallway, book in hand. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Several Royal Courtiers, Several Citizens Citizens are cheering and making noise. In the courtiers' stand beside the throne dais, the Royal Courtiers sit chanting. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (chanting, mocking) Agnivesh! Agnivesh! Agnivesh CUT TO EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION ENTRANCE - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh We see a back view of Agnivesh walking toward the Grand Royal Arena with an ancient book in his hand as the massive royal door opens. Transitioning to a front entry view, Agnivesh steps through the grand entrance into the arena, holding the ancient book in hand and a worn ANCESTRAL SWORD hanging at his waist. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Ranvijay's Horse, Maharaja Someshwar, Rajguru Badrinath, Devika, Royal Guard, Citizen, Several Citizens, Several Royal Courtiers Maharaja Someshwar sits on his throne on the dais, a ROYAL GUARD at attention beside him holding the tall royal sun banner. Rajguru Badrinath stands at the front rail of the courtiers' stand. Ranvijay is still on horseback in front of the stand. From his saddle, Ranvijay turns towards the south gate. AGNIVESH walks across the sand toward him, reading the book in his hand, the worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist. PRINCE RANVIJAY (calling down, taunting, laughing) jise tum sab yuddh ke liye bula rahe ho vo koi yoddha nahi balki ek durbal aur kaayar naari ke samaan hai.... Rajguru Badrinath turns from the courtiers' stand toward the Maharaja on the dais. RAJGURU BADRINATH (soft, poisonous) kaayaron ko yuddh se door hi rakhna chahiye maharaj. Main aapse anurodh karta hun Yuvraj Ranvijay ko is rajya ka hone wala samraat ghoshit kiya jaaye. The citizens laugh at him and whisper to each other. A CITIZEN leaning over the railing of the stone stands calls out. CITIZEN (mocking) haar ke dar se.. haath mein kitaab leke aaya hai... Agnivesh stops on the sand in front of Ranvijay's horse, just below the throne dais, closes his book, bends down and places it on the sandy ground. He rises, looks up towards Maharaja Someshwar on the dais and greets him with folded hands. For a split second, his right sleeve shifts up, revealing a faint golden SWORD-SHAPED MARK on his wrist. He tugs the sleeve back down. AGNIVESH (steady, respectful) Pranaam Pitashri. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (hard, loud) HUH... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (feeling agony) Tujh jaise kaayar aur darpook insaan ko apna putra kahna .. aa thuuu.. ye mera aur poori praja ka apmaan hai.. Agnivesh straightens. The citizens are quiet now. AGNIVESH (low, controlled) Pitashri..Yeh mera bhi rajya hai aur main is rajya ka vaasi hu..mujhe bhi apna samarthya dikhaane ka mauka milna chahiye Agnivesh turns to his brother Ranvijay, places his right fist and draws the ANCESTRAL SWORD from its sheath. His wrist mark flares beneath his sleeve, a jolt runs up his arm, and the sword slips from his hand and falls. everyone starts laughing loudly, Maharaja Someshwar also feeling the same. PRINCE RANVIJAY (laughing, sharp) ye tera rajya hai na?....to Ja aur rajya ke logo ka mal mootra saaf kar ke rajya ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar. kyunki tujh jaise insaan se yuddh karna to mere liye hi apmaan ki baat hai.. RAJGURU BADRINATH (arrogent, public) Rajkumar ek dam sahi kah rahe hain. Mrityu Grahan mein janma balak na to rajya ka varis ho skata hai aur na hi is pratiyogita me bhaag le sakta hai.., yahi niyam hai. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (murmuring, uneasy) Mrityu Grahan ... awwww.. kya ye sach hai? AGNIVESH (firm, restrained) janm se koi bhi apraadhi nahi hota raajguru, aur na hi janm lena koi apraadh hai. Agnivesh looks towards Maharaja Someshwar Maharaja Someshwar rises from his throne in anger, towering over Agnivesh from the dais. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, cutting) Tu janm lete hi apni maa ko nigal gya .. yahi tera sabse bada apraadh hai. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (louder, cruelly formal) Tujhe is Rajmahal aur is rajya mein bas teri mari hui maa aur meri kripa ki wajah se rahne diya gaya hai. Agnivesh falls down on his knees just right besides the Ancestor Sword, he joins his hands and starts pleading to his father Maharaja Someshwar. AGNIVESH (voice tight, respectful) Aapko poori praja ke saamne yun mera uphaas nahi karna chahiye maharaj. Maharaja Someshwar raises his hand. The ROYAL GUARD beside the throne lowers the royal sun banner. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, public) main Iss rajya ka Maharaj, tujhe ye aadesh deta hun...ki tu apni maa ki ye mahaan talwaar abhi Ranvijay ko saunp de. ye talwaar ek sacche rajkumaar ke haath mein hi shobha deti hai naaki tujh jaise kaayar aur shraapit insaan ke... Agnivesh picks up his sword, gets up and grips the hilt. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Ranvijay steps down from his horse, walks towards Agnivesh and holds out his palm without looking at Agnivesh. PRINCE RANVIJAY (quiet, arrogant) Ye talwaar mujhe de de Agnivesh.. AGNIVESH (voice deep, controlled) Ye talwaar tumhe sweekar hi nahi karegi..kyuki tum iske laayak hi nahi ho. In fear that a fight might break out between the two, the people standing around start breaking out in a nervous sweat. Everybody looking at Ranvijay’s open palm. Maharaja Someshwar steps forward to the edge of the dais and points his finger at Agnivesh. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (anger , shouting) Agnivesh........... Talwar Ranvijay ko saunp do anyatha tumhe abhi mrityu dand diya jaayega.. A pause. Someshwar surveys the whole arena. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, final) Ab koi pratiyogita nahi hogi.kyuki tum pratiyogita ke kaabil hi nahi ho. yahi hamara antim nirnay hai. Agnivesh slowly raises the ANCESTRAL SWORD, holds it upright before his chest, then lays it across Ranvijay’s waiting palms. Ranvijay closes his fingers around the sword. He raises it for the court. PRINCE RANVIJAY (triumphant, loud) aakhirkar is talwaar ko apna asli maalik mil hi gaya.. The citizens and royal courtiers laugh at Agnivesh. Among the laughing courtiers in the stand behind the Rajguru, one does not smile: DEVIKA (22, turquoise-and-gold warrior attire, a short curved dagger at her belt), the Rajguru's niece. Her eyes stay on Agnivesh. Agnivesh lowers his empty hand. CLOSE ON his right wrist: his sleeve slides back, revealing the SWORD-SHAPED MARK burning molten gold, its heat scorching the silk cuff. HARD CUT

Citizens wear simple cotton dhotis and sarees; courtiers wear silk angavastrams and turbans. Citizens press against the arena railing and raise sun-emblem flags. PRINCE RANVIJAY (early 20s, fair-to-wheatish skin, broad shoulders, wearing golden royal armour and a small crownlet) rides into the arena on RANVIJAY'S HORSE (a jet-black Marwari stallion, red-and-gold saddle cloth). He trots across the sand toward the north end. Brass bells on the reins ring. Ranvijay raises his jeweled sword toward the crowd. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Dekho dekho kaun aaya...Suryagarh ka sher aaya...Rajkumar Ranvijay ki jay, Rajkumar Ranvijay ki jay Prince Ranvijay halts his horse in front of the royal courtier seating area and looks towards the stand. PRINCE RANVIJAY (booming, playful) Dekha, rajguru? mere aagman bhar se hi praja mein sahas aur utsaah ki lahar daud gayi.. Standing at the front rail of the courtiers' stand, closest to the throne dais, is RAJGURU BADRINATH (60s, bald, flame-and-lotus scalp tattoo, white beard, saffron robes, rudraksha beads) who raises both hands toward Ranvijay. RAJGURU BADRINATH (smooth, ceremonial) ye toh hona hi tha rajkumar, sampoorna rajya is baat ko bhalibhati jaanta hai ki Swarnadweep ke asli rakshak aap hi hai. PRINCE RANVIJAY (loud, smug) rakshak nahi rajguru ..main is rajya ka hone wala samraat hun aur ye praja meri daas... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (60s, dusky skin, weathered face, gold robes and silver beard) sits on his throne on the raised dais beneath the sun-carved canopy, just beside the courtiers' stand, looking down at Ranvijay. He strikes the armrest with his ring. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, formal) swagat kijiye aapke hone wale samraat ka.. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR points his hands towards Ranvijay, Their eyes meet and both smile. The citizens start cheering his name again. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jay! Ranvijay raises his hands and takes their appreciation. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, formal) Poore rajya mein koi hai jo Yuvraj Ranvijay ko chunauti de sake? EXT. RAJMAHAL - DAY (CONTINUOUS) We see the sprawling view of a grand royal palace with endless rooms. INT. RAJMAHAL - AGNIVESH'S READING ROOM - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh A quiet room filled with bookshelves lined with ancient books. AGNIVESH (24, royal-blue angrakha, ivory dhoti, maroon angavastram, worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist) sits in shadow by a narrow window, slowly turning the pages of an ancient book. Hearing the distant roar from the arena, Agnivesh closes the book, rises and walks out through the hallway, book in hand. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Several Royal Courtiers, Several Citizens Citizens are cheering and making noise. In the courtiers' stand beside the throne dais, the Royal Courtiers sit chanting. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (chanting, mocking) Agnivesh! Agnivesh! Agnivesh CUT TO EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION ENTRANCE - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh We see a back view of Agnivesh walking toward the Grand Royal Arena with an ancient book in his hand as the massive royal door opens. Rajguru Badrinath stands at the front rail of the courtiers' stand. Ranvijay is still on horseback in front of the stand. From his saddle, Ranvijay turns towards the south gate. AGNIVESH walks across the sand toward him, reading the book in his hand, the worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist. PRINCE RANVIJAY (calling down, taunting, laughing) jise tum sab yuddh ke liye bula rahe ho vo koi yoddha nahi balki ek durbal aur kaayar naari ke samaan hai.... Rajguru Badrinath turns from the courtiers' stand toward the Maharaja on the dais. RAJGURU BADRINATH (soft, poisonous) kaayaron ko yuddh se door hi rakhna chahiye maharaj. Main aapse anurodh karta hun Yuvraj Ranvijay ko is rajya ka hone wala samraat ghoshit kiya jaaye. The citizens laugh at him and whisper to each other. A CITIZEN leaning over the railing of the stone stands calls out. CITIZEN (mocking) haar ke dar se.. haath mein kitaab leke aaya hai... Agnivesh stops on the sand in front of Ranvijay's horse, just below the throne dais, closes his book, bends down and places it on the sandy ground. He rises, looks up towards Maharaja Someshwar on the dais and greets him with folded hands. For a split second, his right sleeve shifts up, revealing a faint golden SWORD-SHAPED MARK on his wrist. He tugs the sleeve back down. AGNIVESH (steady, respectful) Pranaam Pitashri. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (hard, loud) HUH... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (feeling agony) Tujh jaise kaayar aur darpook insaan ko apna putra kahna .. aa thuuu.. ye mera aur poori praja ka apmaan hai.. Agnivesh straightens. The citizens are quiet now. AGNIVESH (low, controlled) Pitashri..Yeh mera bhi rajya hai aur main is rajya ka vaasi hu..mujhe bhi apna samarthya dikhaane ka mauka milna chahiye Agnivesh turns to his brother Ranvijay, places his right fist and draws the ANCESTRAL SWORD from its sheath. His wrist mark flares beneath his sleeve, a jolt runs up his arm, and the sword slips from his hand and falls. everyone starts laughing loudly, Maharaja Someshwar also feeling the same. PRINCE RANVIJAY (laughing, sharp) ye tera rajya hai na?....to Ja aur rajya ke logo ka mal mootra saaf kar ke rajya ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar. kyunki tujh jaise insaan se yuddh karna to mere liye hi apmaan ki baat hai.. RAJGURU BADRINATH (arrogent, public) Rajkumar ek dam sahi kah rahe hain. Mrityu Grahan mein janma balak na to rajya ka varis ho skata hai aur na hi is pratiyogita me bhaag le sakta hai.., yahi niyam hai. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (murmuring, uneasy) Mrityu Grahan ... awwww.. kya ye sach hai? AGNIVESH (firm, restrained) janm se koi bhi apraadhi nahi hota raajguru, aur na hi janm lena koi apraadh hai. Agnivesh looks towards Maharaja Someshwar Maharaja Someshwar rises from his throne in anger, towering over Agnivesh from the dais. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, cutting) Tu janm lete hi apni maa ko nigal gya .. yahi tera sabse bada apraadh hai. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (louder, cruelly formal) Tujhe is Rajmahal aur is rajya mein bas teri mari hui maa aur meri kripa ki wajah se rahne diya gaya hai. Agnivesh falls down on his knees just right besides the Ancestor Sword, he joins his hands and starts pleading to his father Maharaja Someshwar. AGNIVESH (voice tight, respectful) Aapko poori praja ke saamne yun mera uphaas nahi karna chahiye maharaj. Maharaja Someshwar raises his hand. The ROYAL GUARD beside the throne lowers the royal sun banner. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, public) main Iss rajya ka Maharaj, tujhe ye aadesh deta hun...ki tu apni maa ki ye mahaan talwaar abhi Ranvijay ko saunp de. ye talwaar ek sacche rajkumaar ke haath mein hi shobha deti hai naaki tujh jaise kaayar aur shraapit insaan ke... Agnivesh picks up his sword, gets up and grips the hilt. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Ranvijay steps down from his horse, walks towards Agnivesh and holds out his palm without looking at Agnivesh. PRINCE RANVIJAY (quiet, arrogant) Ye talwaar mujhe de de Agnivesh.. AGNIVESH (voice deep, controlled) Ye talwaar tumhe sweekar hi nahi karegi..kyuki tum iske laayak hi nahi ho. In fear that a fight might break out between the two, the people standing around start breaking out in a nervous sweat. Everybody looking at Ranvijay’s open palm. Maharaja Someshwar steps forward to the edge of the dais and points his finger at Agnivesh. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (anger , shouting) Agnivesh........... Talwar Ranvijay ko saunp do anyatha tumhe abhi mrityu dand diya jaayega.. A pause. Someshwar surveys the whole arena. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, final) Ab koi pratiyogita nahi hogi.kyuki tum pratiyogita ke kaabil hi nahi ho. yahi hamara antim nirnay hai. Agnivesh slowly raises the ANCESTRAL SWORD, holds it upright before his chest, then lays it across Ranvijay’s waiting palms. Ranvijay closes his fingers around the sword. He raises it for the court. PRINCE RANVIJAY (triumphant, loud) aakhirkar is talwaar ko apna asli maalik mil hi gaya.. The citizens and royal courtiers laugh at Agnivesh. Among the laughing courtiers in the stand behind the Rajguru, one does not smile: DEVIKA (22, turquoise-and-gold warrior attire, a short curved dagger at her belt), the Rajguru's niece. Her eyes stay on Agnivesh. Agnivesh lowers his empty hand. CLOSE ON his right wrist: his sleeve slides back, revealing the SWORD-SHAPED MARK burning molten gold, its heat scorching the silk cuff. HARD CUT
