## Director Production Plan: Episode 2 — Khatre ka Sanket

① Theme & Narrative Core

Core Theme: Sovereign authority is earned through internal mastery and duty to the realm. It is never inherited through arrogant entitlement or enforced by blunt terror.

Emotional Spine:

Tier 1 (Suppressed Endurance): Agnivesh keeps his burning mark hidden beneath scorched silk. He takes Ranvijay's insults with a still posture and steady breathing, and keeps his focus on the realm's defence.
Tier 2 (Moral Intervention): The taunts turn physical when Ranvijay touches Devika's lips. Agnivesh breaks his stillness with an immediate, forceful shove and takes moral command of the room.
Tier 3 (Absolute Dominance & Reversal): With the Ancestral Sword at his throat, Agnivesh steps into the blade. As his mark glows and the sword's sunstone answers, he presses the trembling steel away with one bare finger. Ranvijay stumbles back, charges in rage, and freezes mid-stride as the northern symbol flashes violet and every torch gutters.

Exit Takeaway & Expression Strategy: Immediate catharsis as the scorned half-brother shatters the crown prince's show of bravery without ever holding a weapon. It is followed at once by looming jeopardy as the northern ward fails, ending on a hard cut.

Natural Acting Direction (all scenes)
Grounded and real: Every performance is understated and believable, played as if no camera were there. There are no theatrical poses, no stage gestures and no mugging to the lens.
Eyes and micro-expressions over big gestures:
Emotion reads through the eyes, breath, the jaw and small shifts of weight.
Examples: a held breath, a blink when the blade nicks, a glance that lands and leaves, a fist closing out of sight.
Dialogue:
Spoken at a natural conversational pace, verbatim, never declaimed.
Pauses come from thought, not from the camera.
Lines land on the listener's face as often as on the speaker's.
Where intensity rises:
Only for the villain, Ranvijay, and for extreme emotion: Devika's alarm at the breach, Ranvijay's rage and fear at the blade, the charge and the freeze.
Even then it stays believable. Ranvijay's bluster sits over real insecurity, his trembling hand is real fear, and his rage is a man losing control, not a performance of anger.
Stillness as power: Agnivesh is the stillest person in every frame. The less he moves, the more he commands, so the shove and the single finger land as events.
Listening: Every character is alive when not speaking, reacting in real time. The guards are disciplined and impassive until the finger beat breaks their composure.
② Visual Style & Framing Tone (Native 9:16 Vertical)

Vertical Composition Rules:

Native 9:16: Every shot is composed for 9:16 vertical, with all characters fully inside frame. Every camera note ends with "9:16 vertical composition, all characters fully inside frame".
Two side by side at most: Groups of three or more are stacked in depth (foreground, midground, background), never in a horizontal line.
Centre third: Faces, eyelines and key hands (the finger on the blade, the palm on the map, the trembling wrist) stay in the centre vertical third.
Using height:
An aerial drift over the palace domes in the time-lapse (1).
A crane down from the archive vault onto the glowing table (2).
Low angles on Ranvijay's bluster and fear (9, 39, 41) and on Agnivesh's answers and rebukes (5, 13, 33, 44).
Overheads on the map and the circle of men (19, 35, 46), and a high crane as they kneel at the relic (24).
A low angle from the map looking up at Devika and Agnivesh, her face in the top third and his in the bottom third (25).
A tilt and crane up into the hologram dome (26), and a tilt down from the darkened dome to the spinning compass (29).
A crane up as Agnivesh rises from his knee (33).

Composition Style & Narrative Rationale:

Framing-Within-Framing:
The archive's bookshelves and stone archway, the corridor's stone walls and pillars, and the chamber doorway and dome ribs box in Ranvijay and his guards.
This visually marks their moral limits and trapped arrogance.
Symmetry vs. Diagonal Conflict:
Symmetry is held during the ritual reading of the Celestial Ward Map, to show ancestral order.
It breaks into diagonals whenever Ranvijay crosses the space to disrupt it.
Screen Line (continues Ep 1): Ranvijay is always screen-left, facing right. Agnivesh and Devika are screen-right, facing left.

Three-Layer Spatial Separation:

Foreground: Physical barriers: carved table corners, hovering hologram light, the relic's rings, sword hilts.
Midground: The principal players (Agnivesh, Ranvijay, Devika) locked in confrontation.
Background: Deep perspective of the stone vaults, library stacks, guarded doorways and the dome. Guards sit here, stacked in depth.
Cinematography Direction

Camera Movement (mostly motivated, flowing moves):

Flowing (39 of 46 shots): Smooth movement, always motivated by a character's move, a look or a reveal:
slow dolly track-in and track-out;
arcs and circular tracks (around Ranvijay's strut, the hologram table and the relic);
tilts and crane moves for height;
one gentle aerial drift-in for the palace time-lapse (1).
Fast beats (exactly five in the episode):
The doors bursting open (3, snap push-in).
Agnivesh's shove (12, handheld-energy push).
The blade to the throat (36, snap push-in).
Ranvijay's charge (45, fast track that stops dead on the freeze).
The violet symbol (46, crash zoom that stops on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol in frame).
Static holds (two, for emphasis): Agnivesh's calm lines "Tumhe Devika ke hothon…" (16) and "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
No whip-pans, no jump cuts, no crash cuts. No two consecutive shots share the same size and angle.

Pacing Direction (beat by beat)

Principle: Breathe where the story is thinking, accelerate where it is acting. Every insult gets a beat of reaction before the answer. The five fast beats are the only places the cut rate and camera speed jump, and each is followed by a slower shot so it lands.

Sc 1 (1, 4s), breathe: One unhurried establishing image. Let the night arrive fully before cutting.

Sc 2 (2–20, 117s), build in waves:

2 (7s), breathe: The slow crane down lets the audience read the seven gates and the violet flicker before anyone speaks.
3 (6s), accelerate: The doors burst open (fast beat 1). The first jolt.
4–6 (6s, 7s, 6s), steady volley: Strut, answer, accusation. Even rhythm. Hold one beat on Agnivesh's face after "kapti" before cutting to Ranvijay.
7 (4s), reaction hold: The fist and the glow through the sleeve. A silent beat that tells the audience what he is holding back.
8–10 (6s, 6s, 7s), urgency: Devika's warning, Ranvijay's dismissal, the arc around the table. Cut 10 on the interruption, at "samundar se...".
11 (8s), slow menace: Let the finger on the lips play long and uncomfortable. Hold on Devika's frozen eyes.
12 (4s), accelerate: The shove (fast beat 2).
13–15 (8s, 7s, 5s), escalate: The rebuke, the advance, "naajaayaz". Cuts get shorter as Ranvijay loses control.
16 (6s), stillness: A static hold on Agnivesh's reply. The scene's eye of the storm.
17 (6s), threat: The guards draw.
18 (9s), longest breath of the scene: Devika's line, with the brothers' reactions held behind her.
19–20 (4s, 5s), release: The map collapses and Devika walks away, letting the air out before the corridor.

Sc 3 (21–22, 9s), heavy rhythm: Measured, silent, the scrape of the scabbard as the metronome. No dialogue, no rush.

23–24 (5s, 5s), settle: The entry and kneeling. Calm before the ritual.
25 (5s), breathe: The reaction over the map. Let the audience read Devika's quiet hope and Agnivesh's unease in their eyes before the relic wakes. No dialogue, no rush.
26–29 (6s, 5s, 6s, 4s), wonder turning to dread: The bloom, the hologram surrounding them, the breach, the spinning compass. The cut rate quickens slightly as the gate fails.

31–34 (6s, 6s, 7s, 7s), argument: Devika's alarm, with her glance held on "Gaddaar…". Ranvijay's dismissal, Agnivesh rising, "kamzor / darpok". Let each line land on the listener.

④ Scene-by-Scene Emotion & Camera Intent
Scene 1: EXT. RAJMAHAL - DAY TO NIGHT (TIME-LAPSE) (Shot 1 / 4s)
Emotional Target: The weight of the institution; night closing in after the events of Ep 1.
Atmosphere Direction: Monumental, grand, ominous.
Camera Intent: An extreme-wide time-lapse with a gentle aerial drift-in toward the main dome. The sun races across the sky, the shadows sweep, and a bright full moon rises over the domes. The drift stays small so the day first frame and the moonlit last frame line up.
Spatial Staging & Distance: The palace domes sit in the middle third, with the sky and moon in the top third and the terraces and valley mist in the bottom third.
Acting Notes: No characters.
Lighting Plan:
Start on the Rajmahal Exterior plate's golden daylight, with clear sky and long shadows.
Move through a short amber dusk as the windows light up one by one with oil lamps.
End on the Moonlit Night plate: a deep-indigo starry sky, the full moon just above the main dome, a silver moonlight rim on the domes, lamp-lit windows and valley mist.
Scene 2: INT. ROYAL ARCHIVES - NIGHT (Shots 2–20 / 117s)
Emotional Target: Toxic provocation met with icy moral defiance.
Atmosphere Direction: Claustrophobic, hostile, volatile.
Camera Intent:
Opening: A slow crane down from the vault onto the glowing seven-gate hologram, with Devika turning the compass and Agnivesh leaning in (2).
The entrance: The doors burst open on a snap push-in (fast beat 1, 3). Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh on a slow circular track (4).
The insults:
Over-the-shoulder shots and dolly-ins carry the insults (5, 6, 13, 15).
A low-angle tilt up on Ranvijay waving the map away (9).
A slow tilt down finds Agnivesh's fist and the glow through his sleeve (7).
A slow track-out ahead of Ranvijay as he grips the hilt and advances toward the lens, so he grows in frame and the move ends behind Agnivesh's shoulder for the over-the-shoulder (14).
Devika: A crane down from the violet seal to Devika (8), then a high arc around the table as she points to the gates (10).
The lips: A track with Ranvijay up the left side into a profile two-shot of his finger on Devika's lips (11).
The shove: A handheld-energy push (fast beat 2, 12).
The guards: Agnivesh's reply is a static hold (16). The guards are summoned on a high crane-back (17).
Devika parts them: A low-angle push-in as Devika parts the brothers (18). A top-down crane as the hologram collapses into the map (19). A tilt up as she folds it and walks out through the archway (20).
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The table runs from the double doors at the near end to the shelves and stone archway at the far end.
Devika stands at the far end facing the doors. Agnivesh is at the table's right side.
Ranvijay enters from the doors, circles behind Agnivesh to the near end, then walks up the left side to Devika.
The guards halt just inside the doorway, then draw and stride up to stand behind Ranvijay.
Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.
Acting Notes:
Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.
On the finger on Devika's lips, a flash in the eyes, then decisive action. The shove is functional, not theatrical.
Afterwards he is completely still again. The rebuke is level and cutting, not shouted.
Devika:
Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.
When Ranvijay touches her lips, she goes still with cold eyes: no flinch, no melodrama.
She parts the brothers with a firm, economical push, and her line is quiet and pointed.
Ranvijay:
The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.
After the shove, the humiliation flushes into rage, with his hand going to the hilt. It stays a petulant prince, not a cartoon.
Royal Guards: Impassive and disciplined. "Aadesh Yuvraj" is clipped and dutiful, and they draw in unison.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Royal Archives plate: brass oil lamps and wall torches as the warm, flickering key, with deep moody shadows and floating dust in the shafts of light.
The hologram: A motivated soft gold source from table height, uplighting Devika's and Agnivesh's faces and catching the brass instruments.
The violet flicker: The flickering northern seal throws a faint violet pulse onto Devika's face (2, 8).
The doors: The burst sends a draught that makes the torch flames flare and shadows jump (3).
The collapse: When the hologram collapses (19), the gold fill drops away and the faces fall back to lamp and torchlight only.
Faces: Lit by the same flicker and colour temperature as the set, with real contact shadows on the table and floor.
Scene 3: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CORRIDOR - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 21–22 / 9s)
Emotional Target: Simmering hatred, rhythmic threat.
Atmosphere Direction: Heavy, echoing, claustrophobic.
Camera Intent:
A slow track backward ahead of the procession (21).
Then a low track alongside the scabbard tip of the sheathed Ancestral Sword grinding the stone, tilting up to Ranvijay's sullen face (22).
Spatial Staging & Distance: Single file toward the camera, stacked in depth: Devika (folded map and compass), Agnivesh, Ranvijay (sword in his right hand), then the two guards together.
Acting Notes:
Devika: Brisk and purposeful, eyes ahead.
Agnivesh: Calm, eyes forward, ignoring the scraping behind him.
Ranvijay: Sullen. The drag is a deliberate, petulant provocation, with a small sneer.
Guards: Eyes ahead.
Lighting Plan:

Warm pools of torchlight alternate with deep shadow, so light rolls across each face as they pass each torch.
Sparks of light catch on the scabbard tip.

Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).

A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).

The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).

The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).

The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third.

① Theme & Narrative Core

Core Theme: Sovereign authority is earned through internal mastery and duty to the realm. It is never inherited through arrogant entitlement or enforced by blunt terror.

Emotional Spine:

Tier 1 (Suppressed Endurance): Agnivesh keeps his burning mark hidden beneath scorched silk. He takes Ranvijay's insults with a still posture and steady breathing, and keeps his focus on the realm's defence.
Tier 2 (Moral Intervention): The taunts turn physical when Ranvijay touches Devika's lips. Agnivesh breaks his stillness with an immediate, forceful shove and takes moral command of the room.
Tier 3 (Absolute Dominance & Reversal): With the Ancestral Sword at his throat, Agnivesh steps into the blade. As his mark glows and the sword's sunstone answers, he presses the trembling steel away with one bare finger. Ranvijay stumbles back, charges in rage, and freezes mid-stride as the northern symbol flashes violet and every torch gutters.

Exit Takeaway & Expression Strategy: Immediate catharsis as the scorned half-brother shatters the crown prince's show of bravery without ever holding a weapon. It is followed at once by looming jeopardy as the northern ward fails, ending on a hard cut.

Natural Acting Direction (all scenes)
Grounded and real: Every performance is understated and believable, played as if no camera were there. There are no theatrical poses, no stage gestures and no mugging to the lens.
Eyes and micro-expressions over big gestures:
Emotion reads through the eyes, breath, the jaw and small shifts of weight.
Examples: a held breath, a blink when the blade nicks, a glance that lands and leaves, a fist closing out of sight.
Dialogue:
Spoken at a natural conversational pace, verbatim, never declaimed.
Pauses come from thought, not from the camera.
Lines land on the listener's face as often as on the speaker's.
Where intensity rises:
Only for the villain, Ranvijay, and for extreme emotion: Devika's alarm at the breach, Ranvijay's rage and fear at the blade, the charge and the freeze.
Even then it stays believable. Ranvijay's bluster sits over real insecurity, his trembling hand is real fear, and his rage is a man losing control, not a performance of anger.
Stillness as power: Agnivesh is the stillest person in every frame. The less he moves, the more he commands, so the shove and the single finger land as events.
Listening: Every character is alive when not speaking, reacting in real time. The guards are disciplined and impassive until the finger beat breaks their composure.

② Visual Style & Framing Tone (Native 9:16 Vertical)

Vertical Composition Rules:

Native 9:16: Every shot is composed for 9:16 vertical, with all characters fully inside frame. Every camera note ends with "9:16 vertical composition, all characters fully inside frame".
Two side by side at most: Groups of three or more are stacked in depth (foreground, midground, background), never in a horizontal line.
Centre third: Faces, eyelines and key hands (the finger on the blade, the palm on the map, the trembling wrist) stay in the centre vertical third.
Using height:
An aerial drift over the palace domes in the time-lapse (1).
A crane down from the archive vault onto the glowing table (2).
Low angles on Ranvijay's bluster and fear (9, 39, 41) and on Agnivesh's answers and rebukes (5, 13, 33, 44).
Overheads on the map and the circle of men (19, 35, 46), and a high crane as they kneel at the relic (24).
A low angle from the map looking up at Devika and Agnivesh, her face in the top third and his in the bottom third (25).
A tilt and crane up into the hologram dome (26), and a tilt down from the darkened dome to the spinning compass (29).
A crane up as Agnivesh rises from his knee (33).

Composition Style & Narrative Rationale:

Framing-Within-Framing:
The archive's bookshelves and stone archway, the corridor's stone walls and pillars, and the chamber doorway and dome ribs box in Ranvijay and his guards.
This visually marks their moral limits and trapped arrogance.
Symmetry vs. Diagonal Conflict:
Symmetry is held during the ritual reading of the Celestial Ward Map, to show ancestral order.
It breaks into diagonals whenever Ranvijay crosses the space to disrupt it.
Screen Line (continues Ep 1): Ranvijay is always screen-left, facing right. Agnivesh and Devika are screen-right, facing left.

Three-Layer Spatial Separation:

Foreground: Physical barriers: carved table corners, hovering hologram light, the relic's rings, sword hilts.
Midground: The principal players (Agnivesh, Ranvijay, Devika) locked in confrontation.
Background: Deep perspective of the stone vaults, library stacks, guarded doorways and the dome. Guards sit here, stacked in depth.
Cinematography Direction

Camera Movement (mostly motivated, flowing moves):

Flowing (39 of 46 shots): Smooth movement, always motivated by a character's move, a look or a reveal:
slow dolly track-in and track-out;
arcs and circular tracks (around Ranvijay's strut, the hologram table and the relic);
tilts and crane moves for height;
one gentle aerial drift-in for the palace time-lapse (1).
Fast beats (exactly five in the episode):
The doors bursting open (3, snap push-in).
Agnivesh's shove (12, handheld-energy push).
The blade to the throat (36, snap push-in).
Ranvijay's charge (45, fast track that stops dead on the freeze).
The violet symbol (46, crash zoom that stops on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol in frame).
Static holds (two, for emphasis): Agnivesh's calm lines "Tumhe Devika ke hothon…" (16) and "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
No whip-pans, no jump cuts, no crash cuts. No two consecutive shots share the same size and angle.

Shot-Size Variety:

Extreme wide: The palace time-lapse (1).
Wides: The archive and chamber masters (2, 10, 17, 23, 24, 27, 30), the corridor procession (21), the overhead circle (35) and the charge (45).
Full shot: The profile two-shot of both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat (37).
Medium wides and mediums: Carry the confrontations.
Medium close-ups: For the insults and rebukes, and the reaction two-shot of Devika and Agnivesh from the map (25).
Close-ups, extreme close-ups and inserts: Kept for the fist and sleeve (7), the palm on the map (19), the scabbard tip (22), the blade at the throat (36), the finger, mark and sunstone (42) and the violet symbol (46, a top-down close-up framed with a dark margin so nothing crops).
Over-the-shoulder pairs (5–6, 15, 34) and the profile two-shot (37) keep both brothers in every exchange.

Lens Choices & Depth of Field (matching the location plates' full-frame anamorphic look):

Wide and establishing: 24–32mm equivalent, with deep focus so groups stacked in depth all read (for example the procession in 21 and the guards behind Ranvijay in 17).

Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.

The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.

Devika steps between them and pushes them apart. DEVIKA (quiet, pointed) Aap dono ko yahan nahi, yuddh-bhoomi mein ladna chahiye. The hologram collapses back into it, and the map shrinks into a single sheet of ancient parchment. ARCHIVE WARD CORRIDOR - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 A tense procession moves through the torch-lit corridor. Devika leads, holding the folded map and brass compass, with Agnivesh close behind. Ranvijay follows, the sheathed ANCESTRAL SWORD now in his hand, dragging its scabbard tip along the floor and scraping streaks into the stone. The two royal guards bring up the rear. INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 Devika carries the map into the inner chamber. Agnivesh and Ranvijay follow. The two royal guards take position on either side of the chamber door. A SUN-SEAL RELIC, a round golden disc with concentric rings, is set into the centre of the stone floor. Devika kneels at the relic and unrolls the map over it; Agnivesh kneels opposite her and helps press it flat. Ranvijay stands back near the door, arms folded. The relic's golden rings begin to turn. Seven sun-marks rise from the map, and a glowing 3D hologram of SWARNADWEEP blooms above the floor: the island with the city of Suryagarh at its heart, ringed by sea and by seven enormous gates of light rising from the water. Golden beams link the seven gates into a protective dome over the whole realm. Devika spreads her hands. The hologram grows until it surrounds all three of them, the island before them and the ocean all around. At Devika's gesture, the northern gate's doors open, and a bright current of seawater rushes toward the island. A violet crack splits the gate's doors. They jam. The water turns black, and dark mist curls through the opening toward Swarnadweep. The dome beside the northern gate goes dark while the other six gates stay lit. Devika's brass compass spins wildly. The hologram shakes, breaks into streams of golden light and collapses into the Sun-Seal Relic. On the map, the northern gate's symbol keeps flickering violet. DEVIKA (fast, alarmed) Dwaar ki shakti toot rahi hai. Yeh kisi ki saazish hai. Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai.. PRINCE RANVIJAY (flat, dismissive) Bas karo yeh dhong. PRINCE RANVIJAY (furious, rising) Tu mujhe kamzor keh raha hai? AGNIVESH (firm, unblinking) Nahi. Main tumhe darpok keh raha hoon. The two guards close in on either side of Agnivesh. CLOSE ON the blade's edge at Agnivesh's throat, his calm eyes above it. PRINCE RANVIJAY (low, shaking with rage) Ek aur shabd, aur meri ye talwaar tera sir dhadd se alag kar degi. Devika raises one palm between them but does not touch the blade. DEVIKA (hard, urgent) Ranvijay, talwaar neeche karo. PRINCE RANVIJAY (snapping) Chup reh! AGNIVESH (low, clear) Jo maarna jaante hain, vo baatein nahi karte.. aur tere toh haath hi kaanp rahe hain, mere bhai. Ranvijay’s wrist trembles. The ANCESTRAL SWORD shakes before every guard. PRINCE RANVIJAY (strained, shouting) Main kisi se nahi darta! Agnivesh raises a single finger to the blade at his throat. His right sleeve slides back: the SWORD-SHAPED MARK glows gold, and the sunstone on the ANCESTRAL SWORD's guard flickers in answer. With one finger, he presses the blade away from his neck. The sword swings down out of Ranvijay's control; he stumbles back a step in shock. The guards stare in disbelief. AGNIVESH (calm, cutting) Talwaar pakadne se koi yoddha nahi ban jaata. Ranvijay charges at Agnivesh with the ANCESTRAL SWORD raised. Behind them, the scorched northern gate symbol on the map flashes violet. Every torch in the chamber gutters at once. Ranvijay freezes mid-stride. CLOSE ON the violet symbol pulsing in the dark. HARD CUT

A shadow hound turns toward the last standing sentry and leaps at him, jaws wide open. The Royal sentry sees it above him. His sword slips from his hand. He shuts his eyes. Agnivesh throws his spear from behind him. It flies past the Royal sentry and pierces the shadow hound through the chest. The beast’s jaws snap shut just before they reach the sentry. The shadow hound crashes onto the stones at the royal sentry’s feet. Black smoke pours from its mouth. The other shadow hounds stop and stare at the fallen beast. Devika stands by the gate, frozen in shock. The sentry turns to Agnivesh behind him. ROYAL SENTRY (shouting, terrified) Rajkumar Agnivesh! Saare shastra vyarth ho chuke hain... yeh rakt-pyaase pashu kisi bhi shastra se nahi ruk rahe! Agnivesh hauls up the bitten sentry and helps him toward the gate. Devika snaps out of her shock and helps the second wounded sentry through the entrance. AGNIVESH (loud, commanding) Aahat sainikon ko surakshit bheetar le jao aur rajya ke pratyek pravesh-dwaar ko andar se band kar do! Another hound lands on the barracks wall. Its claws split the carved stone and shower the path with fragments. ROYAL SENTRY (panting, panicked) Suryagarh ke mahaveer Yuvraj Ranvijay kahan hain?! Is mahasankat ki ghadi mein humein marne ke liye chhod diya hai?! Agnivesh pulls an IRON SPEAR from a weapon rack on the barracks wall and turns toward the hounds. AGNIVESH (deep, hard) Kisi ka intezaar vyarth hai! Yahi samay hai swayam rakshak banne ka... Apni bhujaon par vishwas karo aur apne logon ko bachao! The sentries carry the wounded through the gate. Devika helps one of them, the CELESTIAL WARD MAP safe in the pouch at her waist. Agnivesh plants himself outside the gate, spear level, between the hounds and the entrance. He paces slowly from one side of the gateway to the other, glaring at the SHADOW HOUNDS. AGNIVESH (cold, clear) Suryagarh ke baahar tumhara raaj hoga... Par jab tak meri saansen chal rahi hain, is dwaar ke bheetar pravesh karne ka vichar bhi— One SHADOW HOUND charges straight at Agnivesh. Two more leap at him at the same time—one from his left and one from his right. Agnivesh thrusts his spear into the first hound’s open mouth. He drives the spear into the ground. The hound dies, its body hanging on the spear. The other two hounds are still in the air. Agnivesh's right sleeve slides back: the SWORD-SHAPED MARK blazes molten gold. He raises his wrist toward them. Golden fire bursts from the mark and turns both hounds to ash before they reach him. Devika and the Royal Sentries stare in shock. AGNIVESH (warning) Bheetar ek kadam bhi badhaya, toh raakh mein badal dunga tum sabko! Seeing their fallen packmate impaled on the spear, the remaining Shadow Hounds hesitate—then retreat into the darkness. Far beyond the hounds, on a black rock at the water's edge, a pair of violet eyes watches. A woman's silhouette (KAALINI) turns away into the mist. HARD CUT

① Theme & Narrative Core
Core Theme: A title can be taken away by decree, but duty cannot. The prince the court calls a bad omen becomes the only one who guards the gate, and his power wakes when he chooses to protect rather than flee.

Emotional Spine:

Tier 1 (Blamed Again): On the temple steps under the spreading crack, Someshwar blames the dark threat on Agnivesh, silences Devika's defence and sends him to the Archive Tower under guard. Badrinath watches; Ranvijay stays behind with the Ancestral Sword.
Tier 2 (The Truth and the Choice): On the tower stairs the silent warning conches raise the first question. Devika's map and compass reveal that the northern gate was disabled from inside the Surya Mandir. She begs him to flee with the map; he refuses: the court exiled him, the people did not.
Tier 3 (The Gatekeeper): The Shadow Hounds overrun the harbour barracks. The guards refuse his command; he takes a spear and runs alone. He saves a sentry with one thrown spear, sends the wounded inside, holds the gate alone, and when three hounds strike at once time stops, the sword-shaped mark blazes and golden fire burns two to ash. The pack retreats, and on a black rock at the water's edge a woman's silhouette with violet eyes turns away.
Exit Takeaway & Expression Strategy: The audience's sympathy for an outcast turns into awe as he finally fights back. The cliffhanger is the reveal of the hidden enemy, not the victory: the hard cut lands on Kaalini turning into the mist.

Natural Acting Direction (all scenes)
Grounded and real: Every performance is understated and believable, played as if no camera were there. No theatrical poses, no stage gestures, no mugging to the lens.
Eyes and micro-expressions over big gestures:
Emotion reads through the eyes, breath, the jaw and small shifts of weight.
Examples: Agnivesh looking down at the silent conches (12), Devika's fingertip on the violet line (15), her eyes welling as she blocks the stairs (37–38), Guard 1 lowering his head (34).
Dialogue:
Spoken at a natural pace, verbatim in Hindi (Devanagari in every prompt), never declaimed. Every dialogue shot stays at or under 2.8 words per second.
Pauses come from thought, not from the camera.
Where intensity rises:
Only for the antagonists and for extreme emotion: Someshwar's fury, Devika's pleas, the sentries' terror, Agnivesh's final warning.
Even then it stays believable. Someshwar is a cold king, not a ranting tyrant. Badrinath says nothing and only watches, hands folded. The guards' refusal is stiff and cold, not sneering.
Stillness as power: Agnivesh never struggles against the guards and never raises his voice on the stairs. His first loud line is the command at the gate (61). The fight is economical: a throw, a thrust, a raised wrist. The speed comes from the camera and the speed ramps, not from flourishes.
Listening: Every character is alive when not speaking. Guard 2 stays silent and does not move when Agnivesh takes Guard 1's spear (36). The wounded sentries are hurt and frightened, not heroic.
② Visual Style & Framing Tone (Native 9:16 Vertical)
Vertical Composition Rules:

Native 9:16: Every shot is composed for 9:16 vertical, with all characters fully inside frame. Every shot line in the prompts carries a "Sides:" note saying what sits in the top, middle and bottom thirds.
Two side by side at most: Groups of three or more are stacked in depth, never in a horizontal line. On the steps the court is layered by height: Someshwar, Badrinath and Ranvijay at the top; Devika on the steps between; Agnivesh and the guards lower. At the gate the three sentries and the hounds are layered from the gate to the beach.
Centre third: Faces, eyelines and key hands (the compass on the map, the fingertip on the line, the spear, the blazing wrist) stay in the centre vertical third.
Using height:
The sky and the steps: the camera rides the crack across the shell (1), pulls back over the whole citadel (2), cranes up the temple steps (3), and lifts up and back over Ranvijay as the procession leaves (9).
The tower: a crane up the stairwell (11); the arch on the top landing with the harbour and the Rajmahal beyond (14, 16–24, 33); the high angle down the open well toward the conches (37, 40).
The POV: from the arch down onto the gate and the shore (24, 32).
The gate: ground-level angles on the stalking and biting hounds (42, 44, 46, 54); low angles on the leaps and the wall-top landing (50, 62); the reverse out to the sea for the charge, the bullet-time orbit and the fire (69–75).
The dome: the cracked Raksha-Kavach is the ceiling over Sc 1, seen through the arch in Sc 2/4, and a faint shimmer over the shore in Sc 3/5.
Composition Style & Narrative Rationale:

Up vs Down: Sc 1 shoots the king from below and Agnivesh from above while he is condemned. In the tower they sit together at the same level. At the gate the camera drops low on Agnivesh once he chooses to fight (65, 69, 75).
Screen Line (continues Ep 3): Someshwar, Badrinath and Ranvijay are top and screen-left on the steps; Agnivesh and the guards are lower, screen-right; Devika is between them. In the tower Devika sits screen-left and Agnivesh screen-right, with the arch upper-right. At the gate the base view looks from the beach toward the gate; the reverse (Reverse From the Gate Toward the Shore) looks out to the sea and the black rock.
The reverses: The tower derivatives and the shore reverse are true reverses, so screen sides flip in those shots only (24, 32, 37, 40, 54–57, 69–75, 77, 79). Track start and end states stay in the forward orientation.
Three-Layer Spatial Separation:

Foreground: The guards' gripping hands and spear shafts, the conches, the map and compass, the near gate post, the impaled hound.
Midground: The principals.
Background: The court and the cracked dome (Sc 1); the arch, harbour and Rajmahal (Sc 2/4); the gate, wall torches and tower on the cliff, or the beach, sea and black rock (Sc 3/5).
Cinematography Direction
Camera Movement:

Flowing moves for the drama: Slow push-ins, track-ins and track-backs, arcs, orbits, cranes, tilts and rack focus, each motivated by a move, a look or a reveal. No slow sideways pans.
FAST beats, Marvel-style (24 shots: 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 36, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 50, 51, 52, 53, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75): the action is cut on short 2–5s shots with lateral tracks, crash-ins, snap zooms, speed ramps and bullet time, exactly as written in each shot. The key ones:
The hounds hit the sentries, seen in a 2s-a-shot run (26–32).
Agnivesh snatches Guard 1's spear and turns down the stairs (34, quick follow).
The barracks overrun: the stalk, the swipe, the bite and the drag (41–45).
The leap and the throw: a fast tilt with the leap (50), then a speed ramp from a fast track into slow motion as the spear flies past the sentry into the hound (52), and a snap back to real time (53).
The climax (69–75): the charge, the fast lateral track with the two leaps, a 180-degree bullet-time orbit while the hounds hang in the air (71), the impact, a speed ramp as the spear butt hits the ground (73), a crash zoom onto the wrist (74), and extreme slow motion as the golden fire leaves the mark, then a hard ramp to full speed (75).
Static holds (8, for emphasis: 12, 46, 48, 54, 56, 57, 58, 66): the silent conches with a rack focus to Agnivesh (12); the dropped sword at ground level (46); the hound landing dead at the sentry's feet (54); the pack stopping to stare (56); Devika frozen in shock (58).
No jump cuts. No two consecutive shots share the same size and angle.
Shot-Size Variety:

Extreme wides: The citadel under the cracked dome (2), the POV onto the shore (24).
Wides: The steps (3), the procession (9), the stairwell (11), the horn (22), the POV of the overrun (32), the gate (41, 49, 67), the dead hound at ground level (54), the charge (69) and the retreat (77).
Mediums and medium wides: Carry the guards, the sitting exchange and the fight.
Medium close-ups and close-ups: For the verdict, the reading of the map, the refusals and the sentries' cries.
Inserts and extreme close-ups: The map and compass top-down (15), the conches (12), the dropped sword (46), the smoke from the dead hound's mouth (55), the blazing wrist (74), Kaalini's violet eyes opening the last dolly out (79).
Over-the-shoulder shots (35, 37) keep the two people in an exchange in the same frame.
Lens Choices & Depth of Field: full-frame anamorphic; 24–32mm wides with deep focus, 40–50mm mediums, 75–85mm close-ups with shallow focus; 100mm macro for the inserts (15, 46, 55, 74); flare only from real light.

Rack focus: from the conches to Agnivesh (12).
Look: Photorealistic live-action, natural skin texture, real fabric, metal and fur. No CGI look, no plastic skin.

④ Scene-by-Scene Emotion & Camera Intent
Scene 1: EXT. SURYAGARH CITADEL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 1–10 / 48s)
Emotional Target: The court's fear turned into blame; a public verdict without a trial.
Atmosphere Direction: Ominous, windswept, the sky breaking overhead.
Camera Intent:
The sky (1–2): a follow shot along the leading edge of the crack (Raksha-Kavach Cracked (Violet Thunder)), first frame matching Ep 3's last frames; a slow pull back over the citadel (Suryagarh Citadel).
The court (3): a slow crane up the steps from the lower steps (Temple Steps, Low Angle).
The plant (4): a slow push-in on Badrinath, hands folded, no staff.
The accusation (5): a slow arc as Someshwar turns to the guards and points.
The grip (6): a slow push-in from the king's eyeline down onto Agnivesh, the city behind.
The plea and the reply (7–8): low push-in on Devika; a slow dolly back as Someshwar takes one step down toward her.
The exit (9): a slow crane up and back over Ranvijay's shoulder as the procession crosses the citadel toward the tower.
Spatial Staging & Distance: Someshwar at the top, Badrinath at his shoulder, Ranvijay beside them (screen-left, top); Agnivesh held a few steps below (Guard 1 on his left arm, Guard 2 on his right), screen-right; Devika on the steps between the two groups; Royal Courtiers in depth by the doors. The guards' swords are sheathed and they carry no spears yet.

Someshwar: Cold fury, sure he is protecting the kingdom. One step down at "Bas, Devika!", no more.
Devika: Firm, not hysterical; she names the traitor inside.
Agnivesh: Looks at the guards' hands, does not resist, says nothing.
Badrinath: Silent, hands folded.
Ranvijay: Grips the Ancestral Sword's hilt as the procession leaves; not drawn.

SCRIPT:
EXT. SURYAGARH CITADEL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Maharaja Someshwar, Prince Ranvijay, Rajguru Badrinath, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 On the wide temple steps, Maharaja Someshwar stands at the top with Rajguru Badrinath and Ranvijay beside him. A few steps below, Royal Guards 1 and 2 hold Agnivesh by the arms. Devika stands to one side of the steps, between them. VIOLET THUNDER splits the sky again; the crack in the golden RAKSHA-KAVACH dome spreads farther from the north. At the Maharaja's shoulder, Rajguru Badrinath watches Agnivesh, hands calmly folded. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR turns to the royal guards. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (furious, pointing at Agnivesh) Yeh khatra is ashubh Agnivesh ki wajah se hi aaya hai! Yeh kaala sankat isi ke paap ka parinaam hai! ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2 tighten their grip on Agnivesh's arms. He looks at them but does not resist. Devika steps forward. DEVIKA (pleading, firm) Nahi Maharaj! Agnivesh nirdosh hain. Dand dena hi hai toh us gaddaar ko dijiye jisne mahal ke bheetar se uttari dwaar toda! MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (grave, thundering) Bas, Devika! Is kul-kalank ka paksh lene ki bhool mat karo... anyatha iske saath tumhein bhi is Rajmahal se nishkaasit kar diya jaayega! The guards march Agnivesh down the temple steps and across the citadel toward the ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER. Devika follows. Ranvijay stays behind, gripping the ANCESTRAL SWORD. INT. ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER - STAIRWELL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2 march Agnivesh up the stone stairs, each gripping one of his arms, a spear in the other hand. Devika follows close behind with her brass compass. On the way up, Agnivesh notices three large WARNING CONCHES mounted on brass brackets at the foot of the stairs. They are silent. AGNIVESH (low, steady) Chetaavani-Shankh kyun nahi goonje? Unke naad ke bina shatru dwaar tak kaise pahunch gaya? Devika raises one hand toward the guards. They release his arms and step back a few stairs up, but stay close. Devika sits on a step, takes the folded CELESTIAL WARD MAP from a pouch at her waist and opens it on the step. Agnivesh sits beside her. Devika places her brass compass in the centre of the parchment map. The compass needle spins, then points to the map. Seven gate symbols appear around Suryagarh. Six glow gold. The northern gate is black. A thin violet line runs from the black gate straight to the symbol for Surya Mandir. Devika follows the line with her finger and turns the map toward Agnivesh. DEVIKA (low, urgent) Uttari Raksha-Dwaar ki yeh rekha seedhe Surya Mandir se judi hai... kisi ne mandir ke bheetar se hi Raksha-Kavach ko nishkriya kiya hai! AGNIVESH (grim, realising) Toh shatru ko jal-maarg se laane mein, Rajmahal ke andar ka hi koi vishwasghati mila hua hai. Devika folds the map and holds it out to Agnivesh. DEVIKA (urgent, pleading) Shatru raj-dwaar tak pahunch chuka hai, Agnivesh! Yeh naksha lo aur jitna shighra ho sake, Suryagarh se nikal jao... yahan ka darbar tumhe sirf ashubh balak hi samjhega! Agnivesh refuses to take it. AGNIVESH (quiet, resolute) Main apni janm-bhoomi aur apni praja ko chhodkar kahin nahi jaunga... Agnivesh rises, determined, his eyes on the Rajmahal through the stairwell's open arch. AGNIVESH (firm) Chahe Maharaj mujhe mrityu-dand hi kyun na de dein! Devika rises too, the map and compass in her hands, frustrated, her eyes on Agnivesh. DEVIKA (frustrated, pleading) Zinda rahoge tabhi toh is rajya ki raksha kar paoge, Agnivesh! Darbar ne tumhe nishkaasit kar diya hai... yahan rehna maut ko aamantran dena hai! Agnivesh looks into her eyes and speaks softly. AGNIVESH (soft, steady) Darbar ne nishkaasit kiya hai, Devika... Praja ne nahi! Pitashri ne keval mera naam mitaaya hai, Suryagarh ke prati meri zimmedari nahi! Suddenly, a horn blares from the harbour. EXT. HARBOR BARRACKS GATE - NIGHT (POV FROM ARCHIVE TOWER) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Sentries, Shadow Hounds From the tower's open arch, Agnivesh and Devika look down at the shore and the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE, which guards the road up to the Archive Tower. ROYAL SENTRIES in bronze armour defend it with swords, spears and shields. SHADOW HOUNDS race across the shore on all fours. Their black, smoke-like fur trails behind them; violet eyes glow beneath lowered brows. They leap at the sentries, snapping their iron fangs and slashing with their claws. A sentry thrusts his spear at one hound. It dodges, bites the spear shaft and tears it from his hands. Another shadow hound knocks a sentry down and pins his shield with its claws. The sentries fight back, but the shadow hounds force them toward the open gate. INT. ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER - STAIRWELL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 Agnivesh turns to ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2. AGNIVESH (urgent, commanding) Suryagarh par mahasankat aa chuka hai! Rakshako, chalo mere saath... Shatru ko rajya ki seema mein pravesh karne se rokna hoga! The two guards lower their heads. ROYAL GUARD 1 (stiff, cold) Maaf kijiye, Rajkumar... Hum sena ke sipahi hain, kisi ashubh kul-kalank ke sevak nahi! Hum keval Maharaj aur Yuvraj Ranvijay ka aadesh maante hain, ek shraapit aur apshaguni balak ka nahi! Agnivesh snatches the spear from ROYAL GUARD 1 and turns to go down. Devika steps in front of him, blocking the stairs. DEVIKA (urgent, voice catching) Ruko, Agnivesh! Apne vaham mein mat jiyo! Akele jaoge toh wah Chhaya-Pashu tumhein zinda chaba jayenge... Aur jinhe bachaane jaa rahe ho, wah tumhari maut par bhi tumhein 'apshagun' hi kahenge! AGNIVESH (low, final) Apshagun hi sahi, Devika... kintu yadi meri bali se is rajya ki raksha hoti hai, toh isse bada aashirvaad mere liye aur kuch nahi hoga! Agnivesh runs down the stairs, the spear in hand, toward the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE. Devika tucks the CELESTIAL WARD MAP back into the pouch at her waist and races down after him. EXT. HARBOR BARRACKS GATE - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Sentry, Royal Sentries, Shadow Hounds The HARBOR BARRACKS stand beside the seashore. Their gate, the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE, guards the shore road up to the Royal Archive Tower. Outside the barracks gate, three royal sentries fight the shadow hounds. The Shadow Hounds rush at them, snapping their iron fangs and slashing with their claws. One Shadow hound knocks a sentry down and bites his lower leg. It drags him across the stones. He screams and drops his sword. Another shadow hound pins a sentry’s arm with its claws, then bites through his sleeve and pulls him away from his weapon. The third sentry backs toward the gate. He raises his sword, but his hands shake. Agnivesh races down the shore road from the Archive Tower, coming up behind the sentries, spear in hand. Devika follows. A shadow hound turns toward the last standing sentry and leaps at him, jaws wide open. The Royal sentry sees it above him. His sword slips from his hand. He shuts his eyes. Agnivesh throws his spear from behind him. It flies past the Royal sentry and pierces the shadow hound through the chest. The beast’s jaws snap shut just before they reach the sentry. The shadow hound crashes onto the stones at the royal sentry’s feet. Black smoke pours from its mouth. The other shadow hounds stop and stare at the fallen beast. Devika stands by the gate, frozen in shock. The sentry turns to Agnivesh behind him. ROYAL SENTRY (shouting, terrified) Rajkumar Agnivesh! Saare shastra vyarth ho chuke hain... yeh rakt-pyaase pashu kisi bhi shastra se nahi ruk rahe! Agnivesh hauls up the bitten sentry and helps him toward the gate. Devika snaps out of her shock and helps the second wounded sentry through the entrance. AGNIVESH (loud, commanding) Aahat sainikon ko surakshit bheetar le jao aur rajya ke pratyek pravesh-dwaar ko andar se band kar do! Another hound lands on the barracks wall. Its claws split the carved stone and shower the path with fragments. ROYAL SENTRY (panting, panicked) Suryagarh ke mahaveer Yuvraj Ranvijay kahan hain?! Is mahasankat ki ghadi mein humein marne ke liye chhod diya hai?! Agnivesh pulls an IRON SPEAR from a weapon rack on the barracks wall and turns toward the hounds. AGNIVESH (deep, hard) Kisi ka intezaar vyarth hai! Yahi samay hai swayam rakshak banne ka... Apni bhujaon par vishwas karo aur apne logon ko bachao! The sentries carry the wounded through the gate. Devika helps one of them, the CELESTIAL WARD MAP safe in the pouch at her waist. Agnivesh plants himself outside the gate, spear level, between the hounds and the entrance. He paces slowly from one side of the gateway to the other, glaring at the SHADOW HOUNDS. AGNIVESH (cold, clear) Suryagarh ke baahar tumhara raaj hoga... Par jab tak meri saansen chal rahi hain, is dwaar ke bheetar pravesh karne ka vichar bhi— One SHADOW HOUND charges straight at Agnivesh. Two more leap at him at the same time—one from his left and one from his right. Agnivesh thrusts his spear into the first hound’s open mouth. He drives the spear into the ground. The hound dies, its body hanging on the spear. The other two hounds are still in the air. Agnivesh's right sleeve slides back: the SWORD-SHAPED MARK blazes molten gold. He raises his wrist toward them. Golden fire bursts from the mark and turns both hounds to ash before they reach him. Devika and the Royal Sentries stare in shock. AGNIVESH (warning) Bheetar ek kadam bhi badhaya, toh raakh mein badal dunga tum sabko! Seeing their fallen packmate impaled on the spear, the remaining Shadow Hounds hesitate—then retreat into the darkness. Far beyond the hounds, on a black rock at the water's edge, a pair of violet eyes watches. A woman's silhouette (KAALINI) turns away into the mist. HARD CUT

① Theme & Narrative Core
Core Theme: A title can be taken away by decree, but duty cannot. The prince the court calls a bad omen becomes the only one who guards the gate, and his power wakes when he chooses to protect rather than flee.

Emotional Spine:

Tier 1 (Blamed Again): On the temple steps under the spreading crack, Someshwar blames the dark threat on Agnivesh, silences Devika's defence and sends him to the Archive Tower under guard. Badrinath watches; Ranvijay stays behind with the Ancestral Sword.
Tier 2 (The Truth and the Choice): On the tower stairs the silent warning conches raise the first question. Devika's map and compass reveal that the northern gate was disabled from inside the Surya Mandir. She begs him to flee with the map; he refuses: the court exiled him, the people did not.
Tier 3 (The Gatekeeper): The Shadow Hounds overrun the harbour barracks. The guards refuse his command; he takes a spear and runs alone. He saves a sentry with one thrown spear, sends the wounded inside, holds the gate alone, and when three hounds strike at once time stops, the sword-shaped mark blazes and golden fire burns two to ash. The pack retreats, and on a black rock at the water's edge a woman's silhouette with violet eyes turns away.
Exit Takeaway & Expression Strategy: The audience's sympathy for an outcast turns into awe as he finally fights back. The cliffhanger is the reveal of the hidden enemy, not the victory: the hard cut lands on Kaalini turning into the mist.

Natural Acting Direction (all scenes)
Grounded and real: Every performance is understated and believable, played as if no camera were there. No theatrical poses, no stage gestures, no mugging to the lens.
Eyes and micro-expressions over big gestures:
Emotion reads through the eyes, breath, the jaw and small shifts of weight.
Examples: Agnivesh looking down at the silent conches (12), Devika's fingertip on the violet line (15), her eyes welling as she blocks the stairs (37–38), Guard 1 lowering his head (34).
Dialogue:
Spoken at a natural pace, verbatim in Hindi (Devanagari in every prompt), never declaimed. Every dialogue shot stays at or under 2.8 words per second.
Pauses come from thought, not from the camera.
Where intensity rises:
Only for the antagonists and for extreme emotion: Someshwar's fury, Devika's pleas, the sentries' terror, Agnivesh's final warning.
Even then it stays believable. Someshwar is a cold king, not a ranting tyrant. Badrinath says nothing and only watches, hands folded. The guards' refusal is stiff and cold, not sneering.
Stillness as power: Agnivesh never struggles against the guards and never raises his voice on the stairs. His first loud line is the command at the gate (61). The fight is economical: a throw, a thrust, a raised wrist. The speed comes from the camera and the speed ramps, not from flourishes.
Listening: Every character is alive when not speaking. Guard 2 stays silent and does not move when Agnivesh takes Guard 1's spear (36). The wounded sentries are hurt and frightened, not heroic.

ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER - STAIRWELL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2 march Agnivesh up the stone stairs, each gripping one of his arms, a spear in the other hand. Devika follows close behind with her brass compass. On the way up, Agnivesh notices three large WARNING CONCHES mounted on brass brackets at the foot of the stairs. They are silent. AGNIVESH (low, steady) Chetaavani-Shankh kyun nahi goonje? Unke naad ke bina shatru dwaar tak kaise pahunch gaya? Devika raises one hand toward the guards. Agnivesh sits beside her. Devika places her brass compass in the centre of the parchment map. The compass needle spins, then points to the map. Seven gate symbols appear around Suryagarh. Six glow gold. The northern gate is black. A thin violet line runs from the black gate straight to the symbol for Surya Mandir. Devika follows the line with her finger and turns the map toward Agnivesh. DEVIKA (low, urgent) Uttari Raksha-Dwaar ki yeh rekha seedhe Surya Mandir se judi hai... kisi ne mandir ke bheetar se hi Raksha-Kavach ko nishkriya kiya hai! AGNIVESH (grim, realising) Toh shatru ko jal-maarg se laane mein, Rajmahal ke andar ka hi koi vishwasghati mila hua hai. Devika folds the map and holds it out to Agnivesh. DEVIKA (urgent, pleading) Shatru raj-dwaar tak pahunch chuka hai, Agnivesh! Yeh naksha lo aur jitna shighra ho sake, Suryagarh se nikal jao... yahan ka darbar tumhe sirf ashubh balak hi samjhega! Agnivesh refuses to take it. AGNIVESH (quiet, resolute) Main apni janm-bhoomi aur apni praja ko chhodkar kahin nahi jaunga... Agnivesh rises, determined, his eyes on the Rajmahal through the stairwell's open arch. AGNIVESH (firm) Chahe Maharaj mujhe mrityu-dand hi kyun na de dein! Devika rises too, the map and compass in her hands, frustrated, her eyes on Agnivesh. DEVIKA (frustrated, pleading) Zinda rahoge tabhi toh is rajya ki raksha kar paoge, Agnivesh! Darbar ne tumhe nishkaasit kar diya hai... yahan rehna maut ko aamantran dena hai! Agnivesh looks into her eyes and speaks softly. AGNIVESH (soft, steady) Darbar ne nishkaasit kiya hai, Devika... Their black, smoke-like fur trails behind them; violet eyes glow beneath lowered brows. They leap at the sentries, snapping their iron fangs and slashing with their claws. A sentry thrusts his spear at one hound. It dodges, bites the spear shaft and tears it from his hands. Another shadow hound knocks a sentry down and pins his shield with its claws. The sentries fight back, but the shadow hounds force them toward the open gate. INT. ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER - STAIRWELL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 Agnivesh turns to ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2. AGNIVESH (urgent, commanding) Suryagarh par mahasankat aa chuka hai! Rakshako, chalo mere saath... Shatru ko rajya ki seema mein pravesh karne se rokna hoga! The two guards lower their heads. ROYAL GUARD 1 (stiff, cold) Maaf kijiye, Rajkumar... Hum sena ke sipahi hain, kisi ashubh kul-kalank ke sevak nahi! Hum keval Maharaj aur Yuvraj Ranvijay ka aadesh maante hain, ek shraapit aur apshaguni balak ka nahi! Agnivesh snatches the spear from ROYAL GUARD 1 and turns to go down. Devika steps in front of him, blocking the stairs. DEVIKA (urgent, voice catching) Ruko, Agnivesh! Apne vaham mein mat jiyo! Akele jaoge toh wah Chhaya-Pashu tumhein zinda chaba jayenge... Aur jinhe bachaane jaa rahe ho, wah tumhari maut par bhi tumhein 'apshagun' hi kahenge! AGNIVESH (low, final) Apshagun hi sahi, Devika... kintu yadi meri bali se is rajya ki raksha hoti hai, toh isse bada aashirvaad mere liye aur kuch nahi hoga! Agnivesh runs down the stairs, the spear in hand, toward the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE. Devika tucks the CELESTIAL WARD MAP back into the pouch at her waist and races down after him. EXT. HARBOR BARRACKS GATE - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Sentry, Royal Sentries, Shadow Hounds The HARBOR BARRACKS stand beside the seashore. Their gate, the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE, guards the shore road up to the Royal Archive Tower. Outside the barracks gate, three royal sentries fight the shadow hounds. The Shadow Hounds rush at them, snapping their iron fangs and slashing with their claws. One Shadow hound knocks a sentry down and bites his lower leg. It drags him across the stones. He screams and drops his sword. Another shadow hound pins a sentry’s arm with its claws, then bites through his sleeve and pulls him away from his weapon. The third sentry backs toward the gate. He raises his sword, but his hands shake. Agnivesh races down the shore road from the Archive Tower, coming up behind the sentries, spear in hand. Devika follows. A shadow hound turns toward the last standing sentry and leaps at him, jaws wide open. The Royal sentry sees it above him. His sword slips from his hand. He shuts his eyes. Agnivesh throws his spear from behind him. It flies past the Royal sentry and pierces the shadow hound through the chest. The beast’s jaws snap shut just before they reach the sentry. The shadow hound crashes onto the stones at the royal sentry’s feet. Black smoke pours from its mouth. The other shadow hounds stop and stare at the fallen beast. Devika stands by the gate, frozen in shock. The sentry turns to Agnivesh behind him. ROYAL SENTRY (shouting, terrified) Rajkumar Agnivesh! Saare shastra vyarth ho chuke hain... yeh rakt-pyaase pashu kisi bhi shastra se nahi ruk rahe! Agnivesh hauls up the bitten sentry and helps him toward the gate. Devika snaps out of her shock and helps the second wounded sentry through the entrance. AGNIVESH (loud, commanding) Aahat sainikon ko surakshit bheetar le jao aur rajya ke pratyek pravesh-dwaar ko andar se band kar do! Another hound lands on the barracks wall. Its claws split the carved stone and shower the path with fragments. ROYAL SENTRY (panting, panicked) Suryagarh ke mahaveer Yuvraj Ranvijay kahan hain?! Is mahasankat ki ghadi mein humein marne ke liye chhod diya hai?! Agnivesh pulls an IRON SPEAR from a weapon rack on the barracks wall and turns toward the hounds. AGNIVESH (deep, hard) Kisi ka intezaar vyarth hai! Yahi samay hai swayam rakshak banne ka... Apni bhujaon par vishwas karo aur apne logon ko bachao! The sentries carry the wounded through the gate. Devika helps one of them, the CELESTIAL WARD MAP safe in the pouch at her waist. Agnivesh plants himself outside the gate, spear level, between the hounds and the entrance. He paces slowly from one side of the gateway to the other, glaring at the SHADOW HOUNDS. AGNIVESH (cold, clear) Suryagarh ke baahar tumhara raaj hoga... Par jab tak meri saansen chal rahi hain, is dwaar ke bheetar pravesh karne ka vichar bhi— One SHADOW HOUND charges straight at Agnivesh. Two more leap at him at the same time—one from his left and one from his right. Agnivesh thrusts his spear into the first hound’s open mouth. He drives the spear into the ground. The hound dies, its body hanging on the spear. The other two hounds are still in the air. Agnivesh's right sleeve slides back: the SWORD-SHAPED MARK blazes molten gold. He raises his wrist toward them. Golden fire bursts from the mark and turns both hounds to ash before they reach him. Devika and the Royal Sentries stare in shock. AGNIVESH (warning) Bheetar ek kadam bhi badhaya, toh raakh mein badal dunga tum sabko! Seeing their fallen packmate impaled on the spear, the remaining Shadow Hounds hesitate—then retreat into the darkness. Far beyond the hounds, on a black rock at the water's edge, a pair of violet eyes watches. A woman's silhouette (KAALINI) turns away into the mist. HARD CUT

ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER - STAIRWELL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2 march Agnivesh up the stone stairs, each gripping one of his arms, a spear in the other hand. Devika follows close behind with her brass compass. On the way up, Agnivesh notices three large WARNING CONCHES mounted on brass brackets at the foot of the stairs. They are silent. AGNIVESH (low, steady) Chetaavani-Shankh kyun nahi goonje? Unke naad ke bina shatru dwaar tak kaise pahunch gaya? Devika raises one hand toward the guards. Devika follows the line with her finger and turns the map toward Agnivesh. AGNIVESH (grim, realising) Toh shatru ko jal-maarg se laane mein, Rajmahal ke andar ka hi koi vishwasghati mila hua hai. Devika folds the map and holds it out to Agnivesh. DEVIKA (urgent, pleading) Shatru raj-dwaar tak pahunch chuka hai, Agnivesh! Yeh naksha lo aur jitna shighra ho sake, Suryagarh se nikal jao... yahan ka darbar tumhe sirf ashubh balak hi samjhega! Agnivesh refuses to take it. AGNIVESH (quiet, resolute) Main apni janm-bhoomi aur apni praja ko chhodkar kahin nahi jaunga... ROYAL ARCHIVE TOWER - STAIRWELL - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 Agnivesh turns to ROYAL GUARD 1 and ROYAL GUARD 2. AGNIVESH (low, final) Apshagun hi sahi, Devika... kintu yadi meri bali se is rajya ki raksha hoti hai, toh isse bada aashirvaad mere liye aur kuch nahi hoga! Agnivesh runs down the stairs, the spear in hand, toward the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE. Devika tucks the CELESTIAL WARD MAP back into the pouch at her waist and races down after him. EXT. HARBOR BARRACKS GATE - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Royal Sentry, Royal Sentries, Shadow Hounds The HARBOR BARRACKS stand beside the seashore. Their gate, the HARBOR BARRACKS GATE, guards the shore road up to the Royal Archive Tower. Outside the barracks gate, three royal sentries fight the shadow hounds. The Shadow Hounds rush at them, snapping their iron fangs and slashing with their claws. One Shadow hound knocks a sentry down and bites his lower leg. It drags him across the stones. He screams and drops his sword. Another shadow hound pins a sentry’s arm with its claws, then bites through his sleeve and pulls him away from his weapon. The third sentry backs toward the gate. Saare shastra vyarth ho chuke hain... yeh rakt-pyaase pashu kisi bhi shastra se nahi ruk rahe! Agnivesh hauls up the bitten sentry and helps him toward the gate. Devika snaps out of her shock and helps the second wounded sentry through the entrance. AGNIVESH (loud, commanding) Aahat sainikon ko surakshit bheetar le jao aur rajya ke pratyek pravesh-dwaar ko andar se band kar do! Another hound lands on the barracks wall. Its claws split the carved stone and shower the path with fragments. ROYAL SENTRY (panting, panicked) Suryagarh ke mahaveer Yuvraj Ranvijay kahan hain?! Is mahasankat ki ghadi mein humein marne ke liye chhod diya hai?! Agnivesh pulls an IRON SPEAR from a weapon rack on the barracks wall and turns toward the hounds. AGNIVESH (deep, hard) Kisi ka intezaar vyarth hai! Yahi samay hai swayam rakshak banne ka... Apni bhujaon par vishwas karo aur apne logon ko bachao! The sentries carry the wounded through the gate. Devika helps one of them, the CELESTIAL WARD MAP safe in the pouch at her waist. Agnivesh plants himself outside the gate, spear level, between the hounds and the entrance. He paces slowly from one side of the gateway to the other, glaring at the SHADOW HOUNDS. AGNIVESH (cold, clear) Suryagarh ke baahar tumhara raaj hoga... Par jab tak meri saansen chal rahi hain, is dwaar ke bheetar pravesh karne ka vichar bhi— One SHADOW HOUND charges straight at Agnivesh. Two more leap at him at the same time—one from his left and one from his right. Agnivesh thrusts his spear into the first hound’s open mouth. He drives the spear into the ground. The hound dies, its body hanging on the spear. The other two hounds are still in the air. Agnivesh's right sleeve slides back: the SWORD-SHAPED MARK blazes molten gold. He raises his wrist toward them. Golden fire bursts from the mark and turns both hounds to ash before they reach him. Devika and the Royal Sentries stare in shock. AGNIVESH (warning) Bheetar ek kadam bhi badhaya, toh raakh mein badal dunga tum sabko! Seeing their fallen packmate impaled on the spear, the remaining Shadow Hounds hesitate—then retreat into the darkness. Far beyond the hounds, on a black rock at the water's edge, a pair of violet eyes watches. A woman's silhouette (KAALINI) turns away into the mist. HARD CUT

SURYAGARH RAJMAHAL - COURTYARD - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Devika, Kaalini, Several Demon Elites The Rajmahal is Suryagarh’s fortified royal palace. High stone walls surround its courtyard. Carved sun emblems mark the walls and gates. Golden ward-lights are fixed above the gates and along the courtyard walls. The courtyard connects to the Surya Mandir, the grand corridor and the throne room. The main gates open on the south side; the steps of the Surya Mandir rise on the east side; on the north side, an arched entrance leads into the Grand Corridor and on to the throne room. KAALINI (30s, pale skin, obsidian hair pinned with serpent ornaments, midnight-blue warrior saree) walks through the open gates. Behind her march the DEMON ELITES: tall warriors in jagged black armour and horned masks, with glowing red eyes, carrying hooked spears. As Kaalini and the Demon Elites pass, the golden ward-lights flicker. Black smoke curls around each light, and they go dark one by one. Agnivesh and Devika rush into the courtyard through an inner passage on the west side and cut across her path at the centre of the courtyard. Agnivesh steps in front of Kaalini and levels his spear. The Demon Elites tighten their grip on their hooked spears, ready to strike. Devika steps up beside him and looks up at the darkening ward-lights. DEVIKA (uneasy, low) Yeh raksha-jyotiyan use rok kyun nahi rahin? Along the walls, the last sun-shaped lights die out. KAALINI (arrogant, venomous) Tumhare Suryagarh ka suraksha-chakra ab mere aage ek bujhi hui raakh hai, Balika. Tumhari prarthana vyarth hai aur tumhara devta vivash. Yahan ab keval mera raaj chalega! Agnivesh looks at the black smoke spreading across the courtyard stones. AGNIVESH (low, to Devika) Raksha-jyotiyan aise hi nahi bujh sakti... Avashya Surya Mandir ke kisi drohi ne bheetar se mantra-bhang kiya hai! Kaalini steps toward Agnivesh and faces him. The Demon Elites stand behind her, spears ready. KAALINI (cold, dismissive) Raasta chhodo, Rajkumar. Ab is mahal par andhkaar ka raaj hoga. AGNIVESH (firm, defiant) Jab tak Agnivesh jeevit hai, singhasan tak pahunchne ka tumhara ye sapna kabhi poora nahi hoga, Kaalini! Behind Kaalini, the Demon Elites point their spears at Agnivesh. Devika stands firm beside him. KAALINI (mocking) Tumhare pita ne tumhara naam mita diya hai, ab tumhara koi adhikaar nahi iss rajya pe. Ab tum keval is mitti par bhatakte hue ek bhikshuk ke samaan ho! Kaalini glances back at her Demon Elites and nods. They turn their hooked spears toward Devika. Devika steps back in fear. Agnivesh steps up beside her and shifts his spear away from Kaalini, pointing it at the Demon Elites. Devika stands firm at his side, unafraid. KAALINI (mocking, to her Demon Elites) Is parajit Rajkumar ka thoda dhyan rakhna, mere veero... Abhi-abhi Suryagarh se nishkaasit hua hai, komal dil hai bechare ka, kahin ro na pade! Kaalini strokes Agnivesh's cheek with mock affection, then walks away toward the Surya Mandir steps on the east side. Her Demon Elites stay, spears levelled at Agnivesh. DEVIKA (urgent) Woh Surya Mandir ki taraf ja rahi hai! Agnivesh replies to Devika in a low voice, his spear still pointed toward the Demon Elites. AGNIVESH (low, urgent) Devika, dev-sevikayon ko surakshit bahar le jao. Main Kaalini ko rokta hoon! Agnivesh pushes back his sleeve. The SWORD-SHAPED MARK on his wrist flares with a blinding golden light. The Demon Elites stagger back, shielding their eyes, and in the confusion Agnivesh and Devika slip away toward the Surya Mandir. INT. SURYA MANDIR - GARBHAGRIHA - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Kaalini, Agnivesh, Devika, Temple Priestess Leader, Several Temple Priestesses, Several Demon Elites The SUN ALTAR stands at the centre of the sanctum, beneath the golden SUN MANDALA on the far wall. The main entrance is at the near end, a side arch opens on the left wall, and a small rear doorway is behind the altar. KAALINI strides into the sanctum as several TEMPLE PRIESTESSES in white-and-gold sarees form a circle around the SUN ALTAR. TEMPLE PRIESTESS LEADER (mid-40s, silver-streaked black hair in a jasmine bun, ivory-and-gold temple-silk drape, crystal mala) stands at the altar, at the head of the circle, and lifts a SACRED SCROLL over it. The priestesses raise brass prayer lamps. Their flames sputter black. The priestesses gasp. The TEMPLE PRIESTESS LEADER turns to the golden SUN MANDALA above the altar and prays. TEMPLE PRIESTESS LEADER (shaking, chanting loudly) Surya Dev, is vipatti, iss andhkaar ko Suryagarh se door kijiye! KAALINI (flat, contemptuous) Apne devta ko pukaarna band karo. Tumhari chikh-pukaar is garbhagriha ki deewaron se bahar nahi jayegi... Yahan ab sirf andhere ka raaj hoga, sirf andhere ka... The priestesses shrink back from Kaalini. AGNIVESH enters through a side arch, Devika behind him, and levels his spear at Kaalini's back. AGNIVESH (deep, forceful) Kaalini, inko haani pahunchaane ki sochna bhi mat. Yeh saare nirdosh hain. Kaalini turns slowly toward Agnivesh. The Demon Elites run in through the main entrance and level their spears at him from behind. KAALINI (mocking, measured) Nirdosh? Mat bhoolo, inki wajah se tumko apshagun kaha jaata hai! While Kaalini's eyes are on Agnivesh, Devika quietly leads the temple priestesses toward the rear doorway behind the altar. DEVIKA (low, urgent) Sab log is raaste se niklo, abhi! The TEMPLE PRIESTESS LEADER runs alongside Devika. At the rear doorway, she turns and calls back to Kaalini. TEMPLE PRIESTESS LEADER (voice breaking, defiant) Jab tak Surya vansh ki jyoti jal rahi hai, tumhara andhkaar nahi jeetega! Kaalini smiles. She draws her SERPENT DAGGER and hurls it. It slashes across the Priestess Leader's throat. A prayer lamp falls from her hand and rolls across the marble. The TEMPLE PRIESTESS LEADER collapses in the doorway. Agnivesh rushes to the rear doorway and sinks to one knee beside the fallen Priestess Leader. AGNIVESH (voice deep, restrained) Tumne ek rakshak ko nahi maara, Kaalini. Tumne Suryagarh ke pavitra man-mastisk mein vaar kiya hai. KAALINI (quiet, cruel) Abhi toh shuruaat hai, Rajkumar... KAALINI (sharp, commanding) Mere veero, iss ashubh rajkumar ko chhodo aur aage badho! The Demon Elites turn and rush out of the temple toward the Grand Corridor. Kaalini follows them. Agnivesh stays on his knees beside the fallen Priestess Leader. Devika leads the surviving priestesses to safety. INT. RAJGURU BADRINATH (bald, flame-and-lotus scalp tattoo, white beard, saffron robes) stands beside a sun-carved pillar near the corridor's entrance as Kaalini enters. RAJGURU BADRINATH lowers his eyes and steps aside as Kaalini and her Demon Elites pass. Agnivesh runs in. He spots RAJGURU BADRINATH near the pillar and stops short. AGNIVESH (strained, respectful) Rajguru Badrinath, aap yahan khade kyun hain? Use rokiye! Badrinath presses his prayer beads between both palms. He faces Agnivesh without lifting his head. RAJGURU BADRINATH (low, trembling) Maine hi Kaalini ka raasta khola tha. Agar main aisa nahi karta toh Timiraksha mere poore parivaar ko maar deta. Agnivesh takes one hard step toward him. AGNIVESH (deep, wounded) Aapne is rajya ki raksha ki kasam khaayi thi. Aur aapne apne parivaar ko bachane ke liye... Suryagarh ke hazaaron parivaaron ki jaan khatre mein daal di. Suryagarh ki mitti par tera yeh andhera kabhi nahi tikne doonga main! Kaalini stands and lifts her dagger for all to see. KAALINI (triumphant) Tumhare rajya ka ant ho chuka hai, rajya se nikaale hue Rajkumar! Timiraksha apna raj-bali lene aa raha hai! Black smoke spreads beneath the throne room doors. KAALINI (calling out, triumphant) Maharaj Someshwar… Timiraksha aapke liye aa raha hai! The throne-room doors BLAST off their hinges and crash across the corridor. ① Theme & Narrative Core
The episode is the night the walls fail from the inside. Kaalini doesn't break Suryagarh's protection, she walks through it: the ward-lights die in purple smoke as she passes, the prayer lamps gutter out, and the throne-room doors blast open for her. Agnivesh, disowned and named ill-omened, is the only one who stands in her way, and in each scene he's held back a step too late: by her mockery in the courtyard, by the death of the Priestess Leader in the sanctum, by the spear-wall in the corridor. The core is a stripped prince protecting the people who rejected him. Kaalini's taunts land because they're true (his father erased his name), and he answers with action, not speeches.

**Natural Acting Direction**

Agnivesh: still and contained. His power shows in what he holds back: he doesn't flinch when Kaalini strokes his cheek (28), and his line over the Priestess Leader is quiet (51). He lets go only on the last threat about his father (69).
Kaalini: never shouts. Her cruelty is in her ease: she walks, smiles and almost whispers. Her only raised moments are the triumphant lines in the corridor (67, 70), and even those stay under a scream.
Devika: real fear when the spears swing to her (25), then she stands firm beside him. In the sanctum she's quick and quiet, an organiser rather than a fighter (44).
Temple Priestess Leader: shaking but loud in prayer (37); her last line breaks but doesn't collapse (45).
Royal Guard 3: a messenger out of breath, not a soldier giving a speech (3).
Badrinath: a silent figure by a pillar who doesn't react (56). No look to camera, no guilty acting.
Dialogue: all 26 script lines (30 Devanagari segments) verbatim, at or under 2.8 words per second.

① Theme & Narrative Core
The episode is the night the walls fail from the inside. Kaalini doesn't break Suryagarh's protection, she walks through it: the ward-lights die in purple smoke as she passes, the prayer lamps gutter out, and the throne-room doors blast open for her. Agnivesh, disowned and named ill-omened, is the only one who stands in her way, and in each scene he's held back a step too late: by her mockery in the courtyard, by the death of the Priestess Leader in the sanctum, by the spear-wall in the corridor. The core is a stripped prince protecting the people who rejected him. Kaalini's taunts land because they're true (his father erased his name), and he answers with action, not speeches.

Agnivesh: still and contained. His power shows in what he holds back: he doesn't flinch when Kaalini strokes his cheek (28), and his line over the Priestess Leader is quiet (51). He lets go only on the last threat about his father (69).
Kaalini: never shouts. Her cruelty is in her ease: she walks, smiles and almost whispers. Her only raised moments are the triumphant lines in the corridor (67, 70), and even those stay under a scream.
Devika: real fear when the spears swing to her (25), then she stands firm beside him. In the sanctum she's quick and quiet, an organiser rather than a fighter (44).
Temple Priestess Leader: shaking but loud in prayer (37); her last line breaks but doesn't collapse (45).
Royal Guard 3: a messenger out of breath, not a soldier giving a speech (3).
Badrinath: a silent figure by a pillar who doesn't react (56). No look to camera, no guilty acting.

Shadow Hounds trail purple smoke, leak it when hurt, and dissolve into it when killed (the impaled hound dissolves at 5).

The blood seal is black with a blood-red glow pulsing inside it (63).
